Policy: Climate Law 2023
Policy_Content: Following up on the 2022 first draft of Israel’s historic Climate Law, the Ministry of Environmental Protection presented in February 2023 a new text to reach carbon neutrality by 2050. The new bill anchors reduction targets for 2030 and states that the annual amount of greenhouse gas emissions in 2030 will be reduced by 50% compared to 2015 (reference year).

Policy: Expansion of nuclear capacities
Policy_Content: In line with the National Energy Strategy, two new 1200 MW units will be added to the Paks Nuclear Power Plant. The new blocks could enter the system around 2030.

Policy: Diversification and strengthening of electrical interconnections
Policy_Content: 'Adriatic link: CC connection between Abruzzo and Marche was authorized by decree of January 31, 2024, scheduled for operation in 2028. Adriatic backbone (Foggia – Villanova power line) is in the authorization phase with operation scheduled for 2028-30. Montecorvino – Avellino Nord – Benevento power line in the planning phase with operation scheduled for 2028/29. Reorganization of the northern Calabria network in the planning phase with operation scheduled for 2030. Aliano – Montecorvino electrode planned with operation scheduled for 2032. Northern Benevento area power line planned with operation scheduled for 2035.

Policy: GX: Green Transformation Policy: Carbon Levy
Policy_Content: Through its GX (Green Transformation) Basic Policy, Japan aims to introduce a carbon levy on fossil fuel imports on power, gas and oil companies.The introduction of this levy will start in 2028, along with a mandatory national ETS.

Policy: Low-Carbon Hydrogen Development Program (PHBC)
Policy_Content: The law aims to promote the use of low-carbon hydrogen in industry and heavy transport, with a capped budget of BRL 18.3 billion for 2028-2032.

Policy: 2025-2027 Medium Term Plan - Turkish Emission Trading System (TR ETS)
Policy_Content: The Plan has explicit references to the creation of an Turkish Emission Trading System (TR ETS), expected to launch as pilot in 2026 and full compliance in 2027.

Policy: CAFE III and CAFE IV CO2 standards for light-duty vehicles from 2027 to 2032
Policy_Content: As of April 2025, the Indian Government is currently drafting new CO2 emissions standards for cars, CAFE III (2027-2032) and CAFE IV (2033-2037), which have proposed WLTP CO2 emission targets of 91.7 g/km and 70 g/km, respectively. This standard will be implemented with a super-credit mechanism making it easier for OEMs to reach compliance through electric car sales rather than through conventional ones.

Policy: Directive (EU) 2023/959 establishing a system for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Union
Policy_Content: This directive creates a new emissions trading system (ETS2) to cover CO2 emissions from fuel combustion in buildings, road transport and small industries not covered by the EU ETS. The ETS2 is expected to be fully operational in 2027, with monitoring and reporting to begin in 2025. The ETS2 cap will be set to bring emissions down by 42% by 2030 compared to 2005 levels.

Policy: Greenhouse Gas Emissions Standards for Heavy-Duty Engines and Vehicles-Phase 3
Policy_Content: The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) finalised in 2024 greenhouse gas standards for heavy-duty vehicles for model years 2027 through 2032.Vehicle and engine performance standards cover semi-trucks, large pickup trucks, vans, and all types and sizes of buses and work trucks, and see a reduction from phase 2 of 40% and 30% for medium-duty vehicles and heavy-duty vehicles respectively by 2032.

Policy: Multi-Pollutant Emissions Standards for Model Years 2027 and Later LightDuty and Medium-Duty Vehicles
Policy_Content: The Environment Protection Agency (EPA) published revised fuel economy standards for model years 2027 onwards, with projected reductions in CO2 emissions of 50% for LDVs and 40% for MDVs in 2032 compared to 2027.

Policy: Detailed Procedure for Compliance Mechanism under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)
Policy_Content: the Indian government adopted detailed regulations for the planned compliance carbon market under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS). The compliance period shall start by 2026.

Policy: Finance Law 2025 - Carbon tax
Policy_Content: The 2025 finance law provides for the introduction of a carbon tax in Morocco, set to be implemented in 2026.

Policy: Malaysia Carbon Tax
Policy_Content: Malaysia’s Minister of Finance has announced that Malaysia will start imposing a carbon tax on the iron, steel and energy sectors starting in 2026.

Policy: National Building Renovation Plan

Policy_Content: Determines the preparation of a proposal for the Investment and Development Plan for the Electricity Distribution Network for the 2026-2030 period

Policy: Public Transit Funding
Type: Government spending in active mobility;Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The Government of Canada announced in 2021 it will be allocating CAD 14.9 billion from 2026/2027 and over the next eight years to decarbonize public transit.This funding encompasses various initiatives, including the Rural Transit Solutions Fund, Zero Emission Transit Fund, Active Transportation Fund, and other related programs.The government allocated a 5-year grant in March to electrify public buses across the country.

Policy: Railway Expenditure
Policy_Content: The Swedish Government has proposed a transport budget of SEK 1,171 billion for the period 2026–2037, which will be used to finance both railway projects and other parts of the transport system.

Policy: Regulations Governing the Collection of Carbon Fees
Policy_Content: Carbon tax applies to power and gas supply industries of annual emissions of 25,000metric tonnes of CO2e or more. May submit self-determined reduction plans for preferential rates. Introduction of industry-specific and technology-specific GHG emissions reduction.

Policy: Second NDC of Ecuador
Policy_Content: Ecuador aims to reduce its GHG emissions by 7% by 2035 relative to a business-as-usual trajectory, and up to 15% conditional on the provision of international support.

Policy: Sustainable Aviation Fuel Revenue Certainty Mechanism
Policy_Content: The UK Government has introduced legislation to support sustainable aviation fuel production in the UK through an industry-funded revenue certainty mechanism, to encourage investment in the construction of sustainable aviation fuel plants across the UK. The Bill was introduced on 14 May 2025, with an expectation for legislation to be in place by the end of 2026.

Policy: Batteries energy storage systems auctions
Policy_Content: Brazil is expected to hold an auction in 2025 exclusively to contract batteries and energy storage systems for the electricity sector.

Policy: Draft Ministerial Regulation on Excise Tax Rates - carbon pricing on petroleum products
Policy_Content: The government of Thailand introduced a carbon tax of THB 200/t on petroleum products on January 21, 2025.

Policy: National Transport Plan 2025–2036 - Electrification of Heavy Vehicles
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport;Government spending in charging infrastructure
Policy_Content: Following the National Transport Plan 2025–2036 and the charging strategy, the government will develop rest areas to facilitate the charging of heavy vehicles. The government set aside NOK 1.2 billion in Budget 2025 to Enova to strengthen efforts for replacing heavy vehicles.

Policy: Rail network investment plan 2025-2030
Policy_Content: Morocco is planning to invest nearly MAR 96 billion in projects to expand its rail network in the next five years.

Policy: (Ontario) Recovery of Minerals regulation
Policy_Content: The Recovery of Minerals regulation, entering into force on July 1, 2025, aims to facilitate the recovery of residual metals and minerals from mine waste at operating, closed, or abandoned mine sites in Ontario. Key components of the regulation include: This regulation is part of Ontario's broader Critical Minerals Strategy, aimed at securing a sustainable supply of critical minerals and driving economic growth.

Policy: 2024 Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund and Warm Homes: Local Grant
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The purpose of the Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund (SHDF) is to improve the energy performance of Social Housing in England, on the pathway to Net Zero 2050.The renamed SHDF (Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund) will upgrade a significant amount of the social housing stock to meet an Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) Band C standard, delivering warm, energy-efficient homes, reducing carbon emissions and fuel bills, tackling fuel poverty, and supporting green jobs.The Warm Homes: Local Grant is a new government-funded scheme. The scheme will be delivered by local authorities and will provide energy performance upgrades and low carbon heating to low-income households living in the worst quality, privately owned homes in England to reduce fuel poverty, and deliver progress towards the UK’s Net Zero 2050 target and Carbon Budgets. Both schemes will start delivery in 2025.

Policy: 2025 Budget- Industriklivet
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The 2025 budget has allocated SEK 100 million to support heavy industry in reducing emissions through electrification and hydrogen use.

Policy: 2025 Economic Competitiveness and Industry Support Action Plan
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling;Strategic plans
Policy_Content: The Estonia’s Economic Growth Plan 2025 sets out seven areas in which the government aims to invest to strengthen Estonia’s competitiveness, including resources and infrastructure. Measures include differentiating regulatory fees for energy-intensive industries, establishing new factories facilitating wind energy PPAs, easier accessibility to finance through EIF support. €589M are offered to support industry helping reconstruction of Ukraine, as well as a €50M increase in the Trust Fund to support industrial exports. 12 business centres will be launched in multiple countries to support Estonian companies entering new markets.

Policy: 2025 Sustainable Energy Production and Climate Transition Incentive Scheme (SDE++)
Type: Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The government is expanding support for sustainable energy production through a new round of the Sustainable Energy Production and Climate Transition Incentive Scheme (SDE++), launching on 7 October 2025 with a budget of EUR 8 billion. The scheme aims to reduce reliance on fossil fuels by encouraging investments in solar energy, biogas, geothermal energy, and industrial heat pumps, among other technologies. It functions as a market-based subsidy, compensating only for the unprofitable portion of projects. Additional incentives will be provided in 2025 for projects that ease pressure on the electricity grid, such as electric boilers operating off-peak hours and vertical solar panels that distribute power generation more evenly.

Policy: 2025 VAT reduction on electricity
Policy_Content: Cyprus aims at reducing VAT on electricity from 19% to 9% starting April 1.

Policy: 2030 Industry and Technology Strategy
Type: Government spending in storage;Government spending in hydrogen;Government spending in carbon capture, use and storage;Strategic plans
Policy_Content: Turkey's 2030 Industry and Technology Strategy aims to establish industrial facilities for nuclear energy, green hydrogen, battery storage, and carbon capture and storage (CCS). The strategy includes setting up clusters for equipment and infrastructure, with a focus on high-tech exports and domestic innovations.

Policy: A Competitiveness Compass for the EU
Policy_Content: "A Competitiveness Compass for the EU" outlines the European Commission's strategic approach to enhancing the EU's competitiveness. A significant part of this strategy focuses on securing a reliable and diversified supply of critical raw materials, which are essential for the EU's energy, food production and industrial sectors.The primary goals of the EU's strategy on minerals are to:Key Measures for minerals:These measures are part of a broader strategy to enhance the EU's economic security and competitiveness by ensuring a stable supply of essential minerals and reducing vulnerabilities in supply chains.

Policy: Act amending Act No. 201/2012 Coll., on Air Protection
Policy_Content: The law transposes the EU Directive on Renewable Energy (RED III) and introduces an obligation for selected fuel suppliers to ensure a minimum share of advanced biofuels, renewable fuels of non-biological origin, per calendar year from 2026 upwards to the level of 5.5% by 2030.

Policy: Act on the Promotion of the Use of Renewable Energy Sources
Type: Ban of gas boilers;Ban of oil boilers;Ban of coal boilers
Policy_Content: The Act states the installation and use of boilers that run on fuel oil, mazut, and coal to be prohibited, except where their use is part of an industrial or production process.Investors who apply for building permits after 1 January 2025 shall not be allowed to install natural gas or heating oil boilers.

Policy: Announcement No. 10 of 2025 of the Ministry of Commerce
Policy_Content: The Ministry of Commerce's Announcement No. 10 of 2025 establishes export controls for specific categories of tungsten, tin, antimony, molybdenum, and germanium materials and their related technologies. The controls are implemented in accordance with China's Export Control Law, Foreign Trade Law, Customs Law, and Dual-Use Items Export Control Regulations to safeguard national security and interests while fulfilling international obligations.For tungsten-related items, the controls cover specific alloys, carbides, and materials with defined technical parameters, including density requirements and elastic modulus specifications. Tin-related controls encompass metal compounds and crystalline forms. Antimony controls include metals, oxides, and specified compounds. Molybdenum controls focus on alloys used in semiconductor manufacturing with precise dimensional requirements. Germanium controls apply to specific oxide and compound forms.Exporters must apply for permits through relevant customs authorities in accordance with these regulations. The controls affect manufacturers and traders dealing with these materials, particularly those in high-tech industries such as semiconductors and electronics manufacturing. The measures took effect upon publication and align with updates to China's export control regime.Key technical specifications include:The regulations include detailed customs codes and technical parameters for each controlled item, along with requirements for associated technical documentation and manufacturing processes.

Policy: Australia NRFC investment commitment in rare earths project
Policy_Content: The National Reconstruction Fund Corporation (NRFC), by the Australian Government to support seven priority areas of the Australian economy, committed significant funding to Arafura Rare Earths Limited for the development of the Nolans Project:The Nolans Project is expected to produce around 4% of the world’s neodymium and praseodymium (NdPr) demand by 2032, creating over 600 jobs during construction and 350 jobs during steady-state operations. This project will be Australia’s first ore-to-oxide rare earths processing operation. The project will deliver significant social and economic benefits to the Alice Springs community, including employment opportunities for Indigenous Australians and local small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The NRFC’s investment is part of a broader capital raise to secure additional strategic investors and funding, emphasising the importance of rare earth elements to modern economies and the global supply chain.

Policy: Australia New Vehicle Efficiency Standard (2025-2029)
Policy_Content: The Australian government legislated in early 2024 to introduce a vehicle efficiency standard to boost EV uptake.From 2025, the standard is set to be 141gCO2/km and to be gradually reduced to 58 gCO2/km for light-duty vehicles. Conversely, standards for light commercial vehicles are set to be 210 gCO2/km by 2025 and 110 gCO2/km by 2029.The standard is expected to come into effect from 1 January 2025.

Policy: BNDES and Finep USD 815 million fund for strategic minerals projects
Policy_Content: The Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) and Finep (Brazilian Innovation Agency) have launched a R$5 billion (Brazilian Reais) public call to support business plans focused on strategic minerals transformation and sustainable materials development in Brazil. Recent operations of large mines have validated the potential of Brazilian reserves for high-volume production of lithium and rare earth elements, leading to increased investments and new world-class project discoveries.The initiative provides funding through credit lines, equity participation, and non-reimbursable resources to invest in productive capacity, research, development, and innovation (RD&I). The programme targets the transformation of minerals crucial for energy transition and decarbonisation, focusing on developing supply chains for lithium, rare earth elements, nickel, graphite and silicon. The support encompasses industrial-scale plants, pilot facilities, demonstration projects, and necessary research studies, depending on project stages and technologies involved. The funding structure is expected to leverage investments five to ten times the available budget in the coming years.The programme aims to position Brazil as a leading supplier of critical materials for energy transition and decarbonisation supply chains. It will support the development of high-value components such as battery cells, photovoltaic cells, and permanent magnets. The initiative is designed to mobilise various stakeholders across mineral-dependent production chains, enabling partnerships between miners and technology holders both within and outside Brazil.

Policy: Battery Booster Package - Industrial Action Plan for the European automotive sector
Policy_Content: In March 2025, the European Commission released an Industrial Action Plan for the European automotive sector, addressing the significant transformation and challenges faced by the industry. The plan outlines concrete measures to secure global competitiveness and maintain a strong European production base through action in five key areas: innovation and digitalisation, clean mobility, competitiveness and supply chain resilience, skills and social dimension, and level playing field and business environment.The package is a key component of the Action Plan aimed at achieving near-term cost competitiveness of domestically produced battery cells and components. The package includes several financial measures and support mechanisms:This package aims to boost European added value, support the entire battery value chain, and ensure a resilient and competitive battery manufacturing sector in Europe.

Policy: Benefit-in-Kind (BIK) Advantages for Electric Vehicles
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The benefit-in-kind taxation for company cars has been significantly reduced for electric vehicles (EVs) to encourage their adoption. According to the updated provisions under the 2024 Finance Act and reinforced by the PLF 2025, the taxable benefit for fully electric vehicles is capped at a lower value compared to internal combustion engine vehicles. From 2025/02/01, the taxable benefit value for electric company cars that are eligible to the environmental score is limited to 30% of the vehicle’s running costs, compared to 50% for other cars. This measure aims to reduce the fiscal burden on employees using EVs, accelerating the green transition of company fleets.

Policy: Bill 5, Protect Ontario by Unleashing our Economy Act, 2025
Policy_Content: Bill 5, titled the is an Ontario law principally aimed at accelerating the permitting of infrastructure and mining projects in the province. Through this bill, Ontario aims to shorten the approval process , in line with Canada’s efforts to the supply of critical minerals.Bill 5 creates governmental authority to designate “special economic zones” where companies and projects can be exempted from provincial and municipal regulations. It also establishes a new mining permitting model that aims to cut government review time by half, grants the government the power to deny mining leases to protect strategic supply chains, and replaces the with a new , among other provisions.The statute could minimise regulatory costs and delays by exempting projects under the “special economic zones” designation, fast-tracking resource development in Ontario.

Policy: Budget 2025 - Financing incentives for renewables including batteries
Type: Government spending in electricity networks;Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending in storage
Policy_Content: In its 2025 Budget, the government allocated €40 million for large-scale battery storage systems, €10 million for incentives to support residential installations of renewable energy systems, including battery storage, and €20 million dedicated to offshore wind and solar projects, complemented by battery storage systems.€82 million were also earmarked to strengthen 82 kilometres of cables across 19 localities.

Policy: Budget 2025 - charging infrastructure for heavy vehicles
Policy_Content: The government proposed funding for charging infrastructure for heavy vehicles, with SEK 930 million allocated for 2025, SEK 605 million for 2026, and SEK 1.155 billion for 2027.

Policy: Budget 2025 - tax reduction on green technology installation
Type: Government spending in storage;Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending in charging infrastructure
Policy_Content: The Swedish Government implemented a tax reduction on the installation of green technologies from 2025: solar panels (20% to 15% from 1 July 2025), batteries (50%) and charging points (50%).

Policy: Budget 2025/26 - Railway
Policy_Content: Indian Railways received an allocation of Rs 2.52 lakh crore in Budget 2025-26.

Policy: COMMUNICATION FROM THE COMMISSION TO THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT, THE COUNCIL, THE EUROPEAN ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL COMMITTEE AND THE COMMITTEE OF THE REGIONS Action Plan for Affordable Energy Unlocking the true value of our Energy Union to secure affordable, eff
Policy_Content: As part of the Clean Industrial Deal, the Commission presented on 26 February 2025 an Affordable Energy Action Plan (COM/2025/79), which is based on 4 pillars: The Action Plan includes 8 actions, many of which will be delivered already in 2025.

Policy: Charging infrastructure investment programme
Policy_Content: Estonia's electric vehicle charging infrastructure with the support of the European Union shall upgrade from 86 new charging stations to 214 charging points built in the country through the funding provided by the Connecting Europe Facility.

Policy: Cheaper Home Batteries Program
Policy_Content: The $2.3 billion Cheaper Home Batteries Program will support Australian households and small businesses with a discount on the cost of installing small-scale battery systems. The program aims to:From , the program will provide around a 30% discount on the upfront cost of installing eligible small-scale battery systems. The discount will be based on the battery’s usable capacity and will gradually decrease until 2030.

Policy: Climate Fund - Hydrogen production at sea
Policy_Content: EUR 380 million were earmarked to demonstrate offshore hydrogen production from wind. First tender for 30-50 MW of electrolysis with COD of 2030. Tender to be launched in Q1 2025. A future tender for a second demo project (with an additional budget) of 500 MW to be developed by 2033.

Policy: Climate Innovation Pull Facility (CIPF)
Policy_Content: Through pull finance, this facility will support innovation, scale up and market building for climate change mitigation solutions for developing country contexts, focusing on innovative clean energy technologies and business models in a small number of specific applications/sectors, where the evidence shows support is most needed. The planned facility is up to £185m, and subject to approvals. If agreed would be part of the Departments International Climate Finance portfolio and funded with Official Development Assistance (ODA).

Policy: Community Batteries Funding Round 2
Policy_Content: The October 2022 Federal Budget provided $200 million for the Community Batteries for Household Solar budget measure to deploy 400 community batteries across Australia.On 2025 ARENA (Australian Renewable Energy Agency) has realised $46.3 million to deploy community batteries across Australia under Community Batteries Funding Round 2 of the Community Batteries Funding Initiative.

Policy: Current Incentives for Electric Mobility in the Megalopolis
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport;Government spending in charging infrastructure
Policy_Content: There are fiscal incentives to promote electric mobility, including exemptions on the importation of electric vehicles, as well as a tax credit equal to 30% of the investment made in charging equipment during the fiscal year, provided the chargers are permanently installed in public locations.

Policy: Cyber Security Law
Policy_Content: The national cyber security strategy mentions that the energy sector is a critical infrastructure. The Act requires entities within its scope to implement security measures, conduct risk assessments, and promptly report vulnerabilities and cyber incidents to the Cyber Security Authority. Furthermore, the Act mandates compliance with standards and potential certification for cybersecurity products and services.

Policy: Cybersecurity Act
Policy_Content: The Hungarian Cyber Security Act mandates energy sector entities to implement comprehensive security measures, report significant incidents, and ensure supply chain security. Regular audits and compliance checks are required to maintain the security and resilience of energy services.

Policy: Cybersecurity Act
Policy_Content: The Act specifically lists various actors within the energy sector that fall under the scope of this law. Actors must manage cybersecurity risks by implementing proportionate technical, operational, and organizational measures and maintain an updated action model. They are also required to report significant incidents to the supervisory authority without delay and fulfill information obligations related to their cybersecurity practices.

Policy: Cybersecurity Act (Cybersäkerhetslagen)
Policy_Content: Sweden Cybersecurity Act (Cybersäkerhetslagen) establishes a national framework to secure critical infrastructure and digital services, including energy services. This law will be updated to comply with the new EU directives in force, namely NIS2 and the CER Directive, to enhance resilience and security in line with European standards.

Policy: Decision No. 266/QD-TTg approving Global Coal-to-Clean Power Transition Statement
Policy_Content: The plan establishes targets and objectives to phase out coal for power generation split in three phases (2025- 2030;2031 - 2040;2041 - 2050), with the objective to decommissioning and using carbon capture for current installations.

Policy: Decision to implement export controls on tungsten, tellurium, bismuth, molybdenum and indium related items
Policy_Content: On February 4, 2025, the Ministry of Commerce and the General Administration of Customs of China announced the implementation of export controls on certain items through the Decision No. 10 of 2025. This decision is based on several existing Chinese laws and regulations, including the Export Control Law, Foreign Trade Law, Customs Law and Regulations on the Export Control of Dual-Use Items. The aim is to safeguard national security and fulfill international non-proliferation obligations.The controlled items include specific materials and technologies related to tungsten, tellurium, bismuth, molybdenum and indium. Exporters of these items must apply for permission from the relevant authorities. The complete list of materials subject to the controls is as follows:Tungsten-related itemsTellurium-related itemsBismuth-related itemsMetal bismuth and productsMolybdenum-related itemsIndium-related items

Policy: Decree 46/2025 on Import Rights
Policy_Content: The decree establishes a tariff exemption for an annually fixed quota of electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles. To apply for the exemption, the cost of the vehicle must be less than $16,000 USD (at FOB value). The maximum number of vehicles that can benefit from this is 50,000 each year.

Policy: Decree No. 1529.24 on energy labels and minimum energy performance standards of air conditioners
Policy_Content: Morocco updated its air conditioners Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS), set to be in force in March 2025.

Policy: Decree No. 1530.24 on energy labels and minimum energy performance standards of industrial motors
Policy_Content: Morocco updated its Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) for industrial motors, set to be in force in March 2025.

Policy: Decree No. 341.K/EK.01/MEM.E/2024 on biodiesel B40 mandate
Policy_Content: This decree sets the biodiesel blending mandate to 40% (B40) starting January 1, 2025.

Policy: Decree for thermal renewable energy auctions
Policy_Content: The ministerial decree promotes renewable thermal energy plants through competitive auctions. It offers financial incentives such as fixed tariffs or premiums, subsidies, and green certificates to support the development of technologies like biomass, geothermal, and solar thermal.

Policy: Decree on the State Program for the Implementation of the Strategy Uzbekistan – 2030
Policy_Content: This decree focuses on expanding renewable energy, including large-scale "green power plants" through public-private partnerships and promoting small hydroelectric plants. It encourages households to install solar panels and reduces the carbon footprint by advancing energy-efficient technologies in various sectors. The decree aims to enhance climate change adaptation, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable resource use.

Policy: Decree-Law 11/2025 - Proceeds with the second amendment to Decree-Law no. 101-D/2020, of December 7, amended by Decree-Law no. 102/2021, of November 19, partially transposing Directive (EU) 2024/1275
Policy_Content: Phase-out of financial incentives for the installation of autonomous fossil fuel boilers

Policy: Deepening the Market-oriented Reform of New Energy Feed-in Tariffs and Promoting the High-quality Development of New Energy
Policy_Content: The notice outlines that from 2025, new energy projects like wind and solar power will have their feed-in tariffs determined through market transactions rather than government subsidies

Policy: Denmark's REPowerEU - Renewable Energy
Policy_Content: The Danish government is supporting the development of domestic renewable energy capacity, notably to boost offshore wind energy generation.

Policy: Development of electricity infrastructure for the development of electric vehicle charging stations
Policy_Content: On March 31, 2025, the application process for non-refundable investment support under the priority program construction/expansion of power networks for the needs of publicly available high-power charging stations.

Policy: ESIF Programme Slovakia - Green for enterprises
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The measure is intended to help small and medium-sized entrepreneurs who do not have the administrative capacity needed to submit applications through demand-driven calls, but also those who could not use the Green Households Program because they also used their family home for business.

Policy: EU funds for Charging Infrastructure- Spain
Policy_Content: Spain has secured €72.7 million in EU funding under the 2024 Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) – Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Facility (AFIF) to expand its alternative fuels infrastructure. Eight business projects approved by the Ministry of Transport will receive support to install 589 electric charging points (150–350 kW), build 26 green hydrogen stations, and decarbonize ports in the Trans-European Transport Network. These grants will help mobilize nearly €400 million in sustainable, low-emission transport investments across Spain.

Policy: Electricity Access Investment Plan
Policy_Content: The Government of Indonesia earmarked IDR 48 trillion for 5 years to reach electricity access for all by 2030.

Policy: Electricity Addition Business Plan 2025-2034
Policy_Content: This plan sets the framework for the expansion of renewable energies in the Indonesian power grid.It states a need for an overall blended investment of IDR 1,100 trillion, of which IDR 400 trillion for transmission networks.

Policy: Electricity Grid Investment
Policy_Content: In the 2025 budget, the Swedish government has allocated SEK 42,601 million for the period 2025–2027 within the investment framework of the national transmission operator, Svenska Kraftnät. Of this amount, SEK 10,319 million is earmarked for 2025. The investments are primarily dedicated to expanding the electricity grid, among other initiatives.

Policy: Emissions limit on the Capacity Market Regulations
Policy_Content: The Capacity Market Regulations emissions limit aims to reduce the amount of CO2 emitted per unit of electricity. The Polish Electricity Networks made the amendment in view of adapting to EU regulations on the fulfilment of emissions limit for units participating in the capacity auctions, expected to start in July 2025. The limit is 550g carbon dioxide from fossil fuels per kWh of net electricity produced. Certification for the auction for 2025 was in September 2020.

Policy: Energy Industry Act - Gas Storage Filling Target Ordinance
Policy_Content: The ordinance lowers national gas storage filling targets to 80% for cavern storages and four southern German pore storages and 45% for all remaining pore storages to be reached by 1 November of each year.

Policy: Energy Renovation Pool
Policy_Content: The Energy Renovation Pool aims to reduce energy consumption in year-round homes in Denmark by providing subsidies for renovating building envelopes and optimizing home operations. Eligible projects include replacing façade windows, skylights, and external post-insulation, as well as installing mechanical ventilation with heat recovery and waterborne space heating. Homeowners, including private homeowners and various housing associations, can apply for tax-exempt subsidies to support these energy-efficient renovations.

Policy: Enhancing the Fiscal Regime for the Large-Scale Metallic Mining Industry
Policy_Content: Senate Bill No. 2826 is a proposed legislative act that aims to enhance the fiscal regime for the large-scale metallic mining industry in the Philippines by amending sections of the tax code (National Internal Revenue Code of 1997) and introducing new sections to promote exploration, production, innovation, and sustainable practices. It emphasises state ownership of all mineral resources, encouraging private enterprise and investments.If passed, it will be applicable to all large-scale metallic mining operations. The bill ensures that the mining industry contributes positively to the national economy while adhering to social and environmental regulations.::1. Mining companies must cover expenses necessary to comply with the following obligations, which are factored into their taxable income:2. : Institutionalisation of an inclusive and participatory mechanism for data collection, verification, public disclosure, and scrutiny of all extractive industry-related data.3. : Disclosure requirements include tax, non-tax, beneficial ownership, natural capital accounting data, and revenue and expenditure data in the extractives value-chain.4. : Establishment of a multi-stakeholder group (MSG) with relevant representatives from government, industry, and civil society organisations.:The Bill is pending at the conference committee to reconcile the differences between the Senate and House of Representatives versions of the bill before it can be enacted into law.

Policy: Environmental Promotion Act (UFG) - Industry Transformation Grant 2025
Type: Government spending in hydrogen;Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The inclusion of the "Transformation of Industry" in the Environmental Promotion Act (UFG) aims to advance the decarbonization of energy-intensive economic sectors in Austria. A total of EUR 2.975 billion is available for this funding scheme for investment grant and transformation grants until 2030.

Policy: European Investment Bank Critical Raw Materials Strategic Initiative
Policy_Content: The European Investment Bank (EIB) announced a new critical raw materials (CRM) strategic initiative to enhance the EIB Group’s role in financing and advisory support for CRM projects across the entire value chain, both within and outside the EU.The EIB adopted a new critical raw materials (CRM) strategic initiative to enhance the EIB Group’s role in financing and advisory support for CRM projects, contributing to the objectives of the EU’s Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA). This initiative includes an expected EUR 2 billion in financing for CRM investments this year. Additionally, a new CRM Task Force and a dedicated one-stop shop will be established to manage CRM operations and advisory activities, increasing technical expertise and partnerships.

Policy: Executive Order 14154 Unleashing American Energy
Policy_Content: The Unleashing American Energy Executive Order establishes a National Energy Emergency and provide a policy framework to encourage energy exploration and production in the country.

Policy: Executive Order on Immediate Measures to Increase American Mineral Production
Policy_Content: The Executive Order outlines several key actions aimed at facilitating domestic mineral production in the United States, citing acute threats to its national and economic security due to reliance on “hostile foreign powers’ mineral production”. Policy: Export controls on certain medium and heavy rare earth items
Type: Export and import ban;Export controls and restrictions
Policy_Content: On April 4, 2025, the Ministry of Commerce and the General Administration of Customs issued Announcement No. 18 to implement export controls on certain medium and heavy rare earth items. This measure aims to safeguard national security and interests and fulfill international non-proliferation obligations. The announcement is based on several laws, including the Export Control Law, Foreign Trade Law, Customs Law, and Regulations on Export Control of Dual-Use Items of the People's Republic of China.The controlled items include:Exporters must apply for licences from the Ministry of Commerce and identify controlled items during customs clearance. The announcement is effective immediately from the date of publication.

Policy: FER-X Decree
Policy_Content: The Transitional FER-X Decree, effective from 28 February 2025, allocates €9.7 billion to support renewable energy plants in Italy with generation costs close to market levels. It offers 20-year Contracts for Difference (CfDs) for technologies like solar, wind, hydro, and biogas, with access via auctions for plants over 1 MW and direct access for smaller ones. The scheme includes regional and installation-specific bonuses, supports new builds and upgrades, and excludes projects already under construction or financially distressed companies. It runs until the end of 2025 or until a 3 GW cap is reached for small plants.

Policy: Fast-charging network investment plan
Policy_Content: Company MH Invest, a state-owned company, is responsible for installing a minimum of 228 ultrafast-charging points in Slovakia along TEN-T network. The project will be implemented by the MH Invest, as the recipient of funds from the Recovery and Resilience Plan of the Slovak Republic, specifically from the Sustainable Transport component. MH Invest, has announced a public tender to select concessionaires for the construction and operation of a network of ultra-fast charging stations for electric vehicles.

Policy: Federal Act on a Secure Electricity Supply from Renewable Energy
Policy_Content: The law comprises amendments to the Energy Act, the Electricity Supply Act and the Spatial Planning Act and the Forestry Act.In line with the Act, if no remuneration agreement is reached, a price based on the quarterly market price on the European electricity exchange will be applied across Switzerland. The Federal Council has established minimum remuneration rates for smaller plants as follows (according to the consultation draft): up to 30 kW = 4.6 centimes/kWh, 30 to 150 kW without self-consumption = 6.7 centimes/kWh, and 30 to 150 kW with self-consumption = no minimum remuneration.In addition, electricity suppliers are forced to increase the efficiency of electricity use.

Policy: Federal funding for regional collaboration on domestic critical minerals
Policy_Content: The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management announced a USD 45 million funding programme in January 2025 to establish regional consortia for developing domestic critical mineral supply chains. This programme aims to establish diverse domestic supply chains for critical minerals by utilising abundant American secondary sources. The initiative emphasises workforce development, community engagement, and regional economic growth while supporting the transition to clean energy technologies. Through coordinated regional efforts, the programme seeks to transform underutilised resources into valuable materials for American manufacturing and defence applications.The CORE-CM Initiative funds six university-led regional consortia to characterise, analyse, and develop critical mineral resources from unconventional sources such as coal by-products, acid mine drainage, and industrial waste streams. Each consortium brings together state geological surveys, universities, private industry, and local communities to identify and prioritise resource development opportunities within their regions.The total DOE funding across all projects is $45 million, with additional non-DOE funding bringing the combined total value to USD 57,469,393. Policy: Finance Law 2025 - Strengthening national energy sovereignty
Policy_Content: The 2025 Finance Bill plans to mobilise 18.2 billion dirhams of public investment to strengthen national energy sovereignty, of which 11.6 billion towards solar PV programmes.

Policy: Financial risk-sharing model for nuclear
Policy_Content: The government proposes a new law on state support for investments in new nuclear power. It outlines the conditions and forms of support, including state loans and two-way Contracts for Difference (CfDs), offering both minimum revenue guarantees and caps on overcompensation. Loans may cover construction, commissioning, and preparatory work, while CfDs apply to regular operations. Support will be conditional, based on agreements between the state and the recipient company, and generally limited to reactors with a total capacity of at least 300 MW at the same site—exceptions may be made. The law is proposed to take effect on August 1, 2025.

Policy: Financing schemes for active mobility
Policy_Content: The government will provide financing support for the following:

Policy: Fossil-Free Energy sources research
Policy_Content: In 2025 budget, the Swedish government has allocated SEK 1.65 billion for research in fossil-free energy, with a particular emphasis on nuclear power, battery technology and hydrogen technology. The nuclear power has been awarded with SEK 400 billion in credit guarantees.

Policy: France-Japan Participation in REE Refining Project
Policy_Content: Japan, through JOGMEC, has announced its support for a project planned by Caremag SAS (headquartered in Lyon, France) to separate rare earths from recycled magnets and raw ores in southwest France and to produce individual rare earth oxides. JOGMEC has decided to contribute approximately EUR 100 million to the project and signed a long-term supply contract that is expected to supply an equivalent of 20% of future Japanese demand for the produced heavy rare earths.France has also provided support of approximately EUR 106 million to the project, including by way of subsidies and tax credits.

Policy: Fundo Ambiental - 2025 electric vehicles subsidy
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: As part of the "Fundo Ambiental", the Government has launched a call of 13.5 million euros to promote the electrification of the car fleet.

Policy: Future Made in Australia Act 2025
Policy_Content: Assented to on February 14, 2025, the Future Made in Australia (Production Tax Credit and Other Measures) Act 2025 introduced tax incentives for renewable hydrogen and critical minerals production, aiming to position Australia as a key player in the global net zero transformation. The legislation recognises that renewable hydrogen and critical minerals are essential components of the clean energy transition, particularly in the manufacturing of wind turbines, solar panels, and electric vehicles.The Act established two primary tax incentives spanning from 2027-28 to 2039-40. The first provides AUD 2 per kilogram for renewable hydrogen production, whilst the second offers a 10 per cent tax incentive on processing and refining costs for 31 designated critical minerals. Both incentives are available for up to 10 years per project. The programme includes mandatory compliance with six Community Benefit Principles, which will be detailed in rules set by the Treasurer following further consultation. Importantly, the incentives are structured as production-based benefits, meaning they only activate once projects are operational and actively producing.This initiative aims to unlock private sector investment in Australia’s renewable energy and critical minerals sectors, creating secure employment opportunities nationwide. By linking the incentives to actual production and community benefits, the programme seeks to ensure that the economic advantages flow through to local workers, industries, and communities.

Policy: GB 19577-2024 - Minimum allowable values of the energy efficiency and energy efficiency grades for heat pumps and water chillers
Policy_Content: The regulation updates minimum energy performance standards for heat pumps and water chillers.

Policy: GX2040 Vision
Policy_Content: The current draft of the GX2040 Vision include specific measures from the 7th Strategic energy plan. Pillars are:- Energy policy:- Emission reduction target of 60% by 2035 and 73% by 2040.- Industry restructuring: upgrading the industrial structure.- Market creation: Create a strong demand for low carbon products.

Policy: Gas boilers replacement by low-carbon heating systems
Policy_Content: Gas boilers in the UK will be replaced by low-carbon heating systems in all new homes built after 2025.

Policy: Government Regulation 8 of 2025
Policy_Content: Government Regulation 8 of 2025 amends the existing Government Regulation 36 of 2023 concerning foreign exchange from export activities and processing of natural resources, with a view to supporting sustainable development and economic resilience in Indonesia. The regulation comes into effect on 1 March 2025.The regulation requires exporters in the the mining (except oil and gas), plantation, forestry, and fisheries sectors, to retain 100% of foreign exchange in a special account in the national financial system for a minimum period of 12 months.Exporters are permitted to use the retained foreign exchange for converting to Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) at the same foreign exchange bank, payment of tax and non-tax revenue, dividend distribution, procurement of goods and services, and loan repayments.Exporters who fail to comply with the regulation are subject to administrative sanctions and penalties, including the suspension of their export privileges.

Policy: Government railway investment plan
Policy_Content: Mexican Government plans investments of 157 billion Mexican pesos for the construction of the first 774 kilometres of passenger railways and 240 kilometres for freight.

Policy: Government spending in rail expansion
Policy_Content: The Government signed a 7 billion euro deal with CFL to upgrade Luxembourg's rail network for 2025 until 2039.

Policy: Grant Scheme for Energy Storage Systems in Combination with Renewable Energy Sources
Policy_Content: The government of Cyprus earmarked €35 million for a Grant Scheme for Energy Storage Systems in Combination with Renewable Energy Sources.

Policy: Greener Homes Affordability Program
Policy_Content: Canada's Greener Homes Affordability Program is part of the Canada Green Buildings Strategy. The program will support the direct installation of home energy retrofits in low-to-median-income households (homeowners and tenants) to reduce monthly energy bills, while decreasing energy use and/or GHG emissions.

Policy: Guidelines for the Use of Domestic Products for Electricity Infrastructure Development
Policy_Content: In Indonesia, Independent power producers are required by Minister of Industry Regulation Number 54/M-IND/PER/3/2012to prioritise the use of domestic products in developing power generation projects, notably renewable energy projects.Minimum domestic product requirements, which were updated in 2017 and 2023, are defined for the development of electricity infrastructure, including geothermal power plants, hydroelectric power plants and, since 2023, solar power plants.Under current legislation, solar power plant modules are subject to a 60% domestic content threshold since January 2024. In addition, the construction of geothermal power plants is to be carried out by domestic companies.

Policy: Heat Network Regulation, zoning and broader policy
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: Through the Heat Network Transformation Programme, the government is enacting legislation and developing policies and regulations to ensure that heat networks can contribute towards reaching net zero. By designating zones where heat networks are expected to offer the lowest-cost solution for decarbonising heat, local communities will have the tools to accelerate the development of heat networks, ensuring that more homes and businesses can access greener, cheaper heat.This includes improving consumer protection, creating the conditions to grow the market, lowering emissions, improving the performance of heat networks, and building up skills in the sector to encourage investment and jobs growth.

Policy: Heat Pump Pool
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The Heat Pump Pool aims to convert heat supply in year-round homes in Denmark to greener alternatives by providing subsidies for individual heat pumps (liquid-to-water or air-to-water). Homeowners, including private homeowners and various housing associations, can apply for tax-exempt subsidies to replace oil, gas, bio boilers, or electric heating systems with heat pumps, meeting specific technical requirements.

Policy: High-Quality Development Action Plan for New Energy Storage Manufacturing
Policy_Content: The High-Quality Development Action Plan for New Energy Storage Manufacturing includes several financial incentives, e.g.:

Policy: High-Speed rail project (Lagos-Abuja)
Policy_Content: The federal government has made an allocation of N250 billion in the 2025 budget for the Lagos–Abujamass transit rail project.

Policy: High-speed rail in Toronto-Quebec City corridor
Policy_Content: Canada is to develop a high-speed rail network called Alto in the Toronto-Quebec City corridor, spanning approximately 1,000 km and reaching speeds of up to 300 km/h. The rail network will connect major cities, including Toronto, Ottawa, Montréal, and Quebec City.

Policy: Home Renovation Programme for the Implementation of Residential Energy Efficiency Investments
Policy_Content: The Home Renovation Programme in Hungary aims to enhance residential energy efficiency through financial support. It offers loans ranging from HUF 2.5 million to HUF 6 million, covering up to 86% of project costs. The programme targets private homeowners, requiring a minimum 30% reduction in primary energy consumption per building, verified by an Authentic Energy Certificate. Eligible projects include energy modernization of detached houses, terraced houses, and semi-detached houses.

Policy: I'm moving electrically C'Cycle
Type: Government spending in active mobility;Government spending in charging infrastructure
Policy_Content: The programme provides subsidies for companies and individuals in order to promote electromobility and sustainable mobility. The subsidies focus on purchase or lease EVs and the charging infrastructure.

Policy: Improvement of energy efficiency and requalification of social housing
Policy_Content: The measure aims to incentivise private investments and improve access to financing for energy renovations of public residential buildings that determine a minimum improvement in energy efficiency of 30%.

Policy: Incentive Tax on Fleet Greening
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: To promote the decarbonization of vehicle fleets, France has implemented a green fleet tax (Taxe Incitative pour le Verdissement des Flottes), updated under the PLF 2025. This tax targets companies with large fleets, incentivizing the replacement of polluting vehicles by zero- and low-emission alternatives. The tax imposes higher rates on fleets that do not meet progressive environmental performance thresholds, based on CO₂ emissions and vehicle types. The evolving framework encourages companies to integrate more electric and hybrid vehicles to reduce their tax liability, supporting national climate goals.

Policy: Incentives for electric vehicles and sustainable transport
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: Transport Malta earmarked a €34 million grant program to support the adoption of electric vehicles, pedelecs, and motorcycles, along with a vehicle scrapping scheme. The initiative is part of the government's effort to promote sustainable transport. The grants for 2025 include financial incentives for various vehicles, such as €500 for pedelecs, €8,000 for electric cars under €40,000, and up to €6,000 for electric motorcycles. There are additional incentives for scrapping old vehicles, with extra benefits for those in Gozo. Businesses and voluntary organizations can also apply for support to transition to electric fleets.

Policy: Information and Communications Infrastructure Protection Act
Policy_Content: The Article 2 explicitly states that the Act applies to the energy sector. Critical information and communications infrastructures are required to establish protection measures based on vulnerability analysis and submit these to the relevant central administrative agency. The heads of these agencies must establish protection plans, and management organizations must notify authorities of intrusion incidents and implement restoration measures.

Policy: Investment credit for large investments aiming at a climate neutral economy
Type: Government spending in storage;Government spending in low-carbon electricity
Policy_Content: Finland offers an investment credit for large projects aimed at achieving a climate-neutral economy, with eligible costs of at least €50 million. The credit covers investments in renewable energy production, energy storage, low-carbon industrial processes, and sectors strategic to the transition, such as batteries, solar panels, and wind turbines. The credit amounts to 20% of eligible costs, up to a maximum of €150 million per company, and must be applied for before the commencement of works.

Policy: Japan 7th Strategic Energy Plan
Policy_Content: The Seventh Strategic Energy Plan outlines policy issues to be addressed in the future and the direction of action under the principle of S+3Es (Safety, Energy Security, Economic Efficiency, and Environment), while taking into account the energy supply and demand structure in 2040 and beyond toward the realization of carbon neutrality.

Policy: Kenya Power Investment Plan - transmission lines
Policy_Content: Kenya Power announced a KES 889 million investment in transmission lines in Western Kenya.

Policy: Large-Scale Equipment Renewal and Consumer Goods Replacement Policy
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies;Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The policy includes increased funding for equipment updates in areas like industrial, energy, transportation, and medical sectors, enhanced subsidies for replacing old vehicles and agricultural machinery, and higher incentives for purchasing new energy-efficient appliances and digital products to have a smart home. There are grants for the purchase of new energy vehicles (NEVs) (passenger cars), with extra benefits in case for scrapping old internal combustion engine vehicles (ICEVs) (registered before 2012 and 2014, in case of gasoline and diesel, respectively) and NEVs (registered before 2018).

Policy: Law 15.042 which establishes the Brazilian Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading System (SBCE)
Policy_Content: The Law establishes the Brazilian Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading System (SBCE), and states five phases:

Policy: Law 327/2021 - Energy Transition Acceleration Program (PATEN)
Policy_Content: The programme aims to foster the promotion of sustainable development projects, connecting financing institutions with companies interested in sustainable initiatives, leveraging corporate credits as a financing tool, encouraging the generation and efficient use of low-carbon energy, and fostering energy transition activities in coal-mining regions.

Policy: Law No 8462 establishing a support scheme for the transition to a net zero emissions economy
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The bill proposes two primary types of financial support to aid the transition to a net zero emissions economy. The first type focuses on helping manufacturing companies electrify their production processes to significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The second type supports investments in the production of key technologies and materials necessary for achieving a net zero emissions economy, including renewable energy equipment and carbon capture technologies.

Policy: Law No. 3769-IX regarding the mandatory use of liquid biofuel
Policy_Content: Ukraine set in its 2024 law its first biofuel blending mandate for road transport.From June 1st, 2025, a mandatory content of at least 5% of liquid biofuel will be required.

Policy: Law No. Zru-987 on the ownership and disposal of subsoil resources, as well as the use and protection of subsoil resources
Policy_Content: The Law sets the regulatory framework for oil and gas extraction in the country. Article 6 declares state-owned property for subsoil and all minerals. The exploitation of these minerals necessitates a permit for the extraction of hydrocarbons, that shall be issued for a period of up to twenty-five consecutive years.

Policy: Law on the resilience of critical infrastructure and the strengthening of cybersecurity
Policy_Content: The Law aims at transposing the EU directive for a high common level of cybersecurity across the European Union, including the energy sector.

Policy: Law to regulate essential principles of information security management in the federal administration
Policy_Content: The Law aims at transposing the EU directive for a high common level of cybersecurity across the European Union, including the energy sector.

Policy: Legal Notice 71 of 2025
Policy_Content: ​Malta's Network and Information Systems Security Law of 2020 (Law 89(I)/2020) establishes a national framework to secure critical infrastructure and digital services, including energy services.

Policy: Local Government fleet renewal mandate
Policy_Content: All new buses and coaches that shall be acquired for public transport services from 2025 onwards must be low-emission vehicles.

Policy: Lower cost of consumer electricity bills
Policy_Content: The Norwegian Government proposes a fixed price of NOK 0.4 per kWh for electricity, effective from October 1, 2025. Consumers can choose between the fixed price scheme or the existing general electricity support scheme. The fixed price scheme offers predictability and stability in electricity costs, making it easier for households to anticipate their expenses.

Policy: Maritime Decarbonisation Strategy
Policy_Content: The UK's Maritime Decarbonisation Strategy was published on 25 March 2025 and sets out the Government's plans for decarbonisation of the domestic maritime sector. It includes goals of zero emissions by 2050, a 30% reduction in lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, and an 80% reduction by 2040 - compared to 2008 levels.The Strategy set out a range of policies that will support meeting the goals including:- Implementing fuel regulations;- Introducing emissions pricing;- Taking action on emissions at berth;- Addressing emissions from smaller vessels;- Improving energy efficiency.

Policy: Measures concerning natural gas
Policy_Content: The public and businesses may be urged to reduce gas use by lowering heating, using less hot water, and adopting energy-efficient cooking practices, aiming to prevent severe shortages in Switzerland.

Policy: Measures to Strengthen the Competitiveness of Eco-friendly Vehicles and Secondary Batteries
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport;Government spending in charging infrastructure
Policy_Content: The Korean government has committed 21 trillion won in 2025 to boost eco-friendly vehicles and batteries. The government invests in the EV and battery industries. Additionally, the programme offers a 20% additional subsidy to individuals aged 19 to 34 buying an electric vehicle as their first car. It also promotes the development of charging infrastructure. Furthermore, it invests in hydrogen buses.

Policy: Medium-term operational plan 2025-2029
Policy_Content: The Medium-term operational plan 2025-2029 quotes R$7.6 billion in investments planned for the period 2025 to 2029 to build and maintain new transmission lines in Brazil.

Policy: Minerals Strategy for New Zealand and Critical Minerals List
Policy_Content: The Minerals Strategy adopts a lens out to 2040, focusing New Zealand’s approach to the development of our minerals estate, with a delivery roadmap to get us there. It outlines actions that will be taken to position the minerals sector to deliver for New Zealanders, focused on three key outcomes of productivity, value, and resilience. The Strategy is guided by overarching principles to honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations and responsible practices.There are 37 minerals included on the Critical Minerals List, which identifies minerals that are essential to New Zealand’s economy. New Zealand has the potential to produce 21 of these, which will enable us to contribute to the growing critical minerals market as a trusted and reliable partner, particularly in the support of global mineral supply chains of minerals needed for clean energy technologies.

Policy: Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) for air conditioners
Policy_Content: The Energy Commission of Nigeria, in collaboration with the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and with financial backing from the Clean Cooling Collaborative (CCC), has been spearheading the Scaling up Energy-Efficient and Climate-Friendly Cooling project since 2022.To advance this initiative, the Federal Government of Nigeria has officially approved and implemented the new Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) for air conditioners.

Policy: Municipal incentive scheme for wind power expansion
Policy_Content: To encourage municipalities to approve new wind power projects and compensate those that have already hosted such developments, the government proposes financial support equivalent to the property tax revenue generated by wind power in the municipality. The initiative is budgeted at SEK 340 million for 2025.

Policy: NaszEauto programme
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport

Policy: National Action Plan for Clean Technology (NAP CM)
Policy_Content: The National Action Plan for Clean Technology (NAP CM) focuses on the development of alternative fuels infrastructure, the modernisation of the road transport fleet and the decarbonisation of transport. The goals and plans set are divided into milestones for 2025, 2030 and 2035.This is an actualization of the first version approved in 2015 and updated in 2019.

Policy: National Critical Mineral Mission
Policy_Content: India has launched a 'National Critical Mineral Mission' from FY 2024-25 to FY 2030-31 to secure the supply of critical minerals and strengthen India’s critical minerals’ value chains. The Government has earmarked an expenditure of INR 16,300 crore (approx. USD 1.9 billion) and expects investment of Rs.18,000 crore (approx. USD 2 billion) by public sector undertakings during the 7-year period.The NCMM encompasses all stages of the value chain, including mineral exploration, mining, beneficiation, processing, and recovery from end-of-life products.: The NCMM sets a target of completing 1 200 domestic exploration projects by 2030-2031, with an aim of ensuring domestic production of at least 15 critical minerals (such as graphite, lithium, potash, REEs). The NCMM also aims for Indian companies to acquire 50 mining assets worldwide. To achieve these targets, it seeks to create a fast-track regulatory approval process for mining projects.: The NCMM seeks to set up an incentive scheme for mineral recycling with a budget of INR 1 500 crore (USD 170 million), with a target of recovering 400 kilotonnes (kt) of recycled material.: The NCMM foresees the creating of a National Critical Minerals Stockpile comprising at least 5 critical minerals to mitigate the risks from global supply chain disruptions.: The NCMM seeks to promote research in critical mineral technologies with a target of achieving self-sufficiency in processing at least 5 critical minerals and generating 1 000 patents across the critical mineral value chains by 2031. It also proposes setting up 4 regional mineral processing parks and 3 Centres of Excellence on Critical Minerals.: The NCMM envisages the formation of an Empowered Committee on Critical Minerals that would coordinate and implement the initiatives under the NCMM.

Policy: National Development Plan (2025-2028)
Policy_Content: The National Development Plan (2025-2028) focuses on population and social development, balanced industrial development, technology R&D capability, net-zero sustainable development and resilience.

Policy: National Emergency to Increase our Competitive Edge, Protect our Sovereignty, and Strengthen our National and Economic Security
Policy_Content: The National Emergency aims at fostering domestic manufacturing within the United States through a subset of measures, including tariff and non-tariff measures.

Policy: National Energy Compact
Policy_Content: The National Energy Compact commits to achieving universal energy access by 2030, increasing renewable energy to 30%, reducing carbon emissions, improving energy efficiency, and fostering public-private partnerships for sustainable power sector development.

Policy: National Energy Compact
Policy_Content: Senegal targets to achieve universal, affordable, reliable, and sustainable energy access by 2025 and increase renewable energy's share in the national energy mix to 40% by 2030. It establishes several objectives and action plans to achieve them.

Policy: National Energy Compact
Policy_Content: The government of Tanzania aims to increase electricity connectivity to 75 percent by 2030 and clean cooking access to 80 percent by 2034. It also aims to increase the share of renewable energy in the generation-mix to 75 percent from the current 61.8 percent, which will require adding over 1,800 MW of generation capacity from solar, wind, geothermal, and hydro. Significant mobilization of public- and private-sector financing is targeted in order to create a favorable investment climate, strengthen local capacities through training, and establish robust data collection systems for informed energy-planning and decision-making

Policy: National Energy and Climate Plan of Ukraine 2025-2030
Policy_Content: The National Energy and Climate Plan of Ukraine sets the policies and measures milestones for the decarbonisation, energy efficiency, energy security and market reforms for the next five years.

Policy: National Integrated Electricity Policy (NIEP)
Policy_Content: The National Integrated Electricity Policy establishes a framework designed to drive a data-driven transformation of the power sector, fostering economic growth and job creation by improving supply reliability for businesses and industries.

Policy: National Plan to adaptation to climate change
Policy_Content: This plan contains measures to protect the population, develop the territory, improve the resilience of our economy, ensure the continuity of public services. This plan is intended to be revised every 5 years according to the reality of the warming trajectory and the evolution of knowledge. The reference warming trajectory for adaptation to climate change so far anticipates anincrease in the average temperature in mainland France of 4°C by the end of the century. With regard to vitally important operators (OIVs), the transposition into French law of Directive(EU) 2022/2557 on the resilience of critical entities will make it possible to integrate thesechallenges into entity planning through the revision of national security directives.

Policy: National Railway Plan
Policy_Content: The National Railway Plan aims for a network expansion of 4,700 km, and shall allocate R$100 billion of both public and private funding to achieve this goal.

Policy: New Heavy Duty Vehicles (Carbon Dioxide Emission Performance Standards) (Miscellaneous Amendments) Regulations 2025
Policy_Content: The UK Heavy Duty Vehicles Emissions and Fuel Consumption Regulations aim at reflecting the EU regulation 2019/1242 in the context of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018.The regulation sets targets to reduce the average CO2 emissions from new HDV vehicles by 15% in 2025 and by 30% in 2030.

Policy: Obligation for the supply of renewable heat (DM OIERT)
Policy_Content: The measure defines the methods by which public and private companies that sell thermal energy in the form of heat for heating and cooling to third parties, for quantities exceeding 500 TOE per year, ensure that a portion of the energy sold is renewable.

Policy: Operating incentive mechanisms to promote renewable hydrogen production
Policy_Content: Article 11, paragraph 2, of Legislative Decree no. 199 of 2021, provides for the issuance of a ministerial decree aimed at supporting the production of hydrogen of renewable origin intended for use in the transport sector and in the hard-to-abate sectors, through the recognition of the contribution to the operating account.

Policy: Order No. 9132/2024
Policy_Content: Determines the preparation of a proposal for the Investment and Development Plan for the Electricity Transmission Network for the 2025-2034 period.

Policy: Organic Law of The 7T Plan (2025-2031)
Policy_Content: The Government has launched the Homeland Plan: The Great Transformations 2025-2031 which covers different topics, including climate change and the country energy mix.

Policy: Plug-in vehicle grants
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: In February 2025, the plug-in van grant was extended into the 2025/26 financial year with £120m in government funding to support the switch to cleaner vans, wheelchair accessible vehicles and taxis. The maximum grant for small vans is £2,500 and for large vans £5,000.The Government also announced that grants for plug-in motorcycles and taxis will be extended into the 2025/26 financial year. The Plug-in Motorcycle Grant will continue at the same grant rate (up to £500). The Plug-in Taxi Grant (PITG) will run at a rate of £4,000 per eligible vehicle.In March 2025, the Plug-In Truck Grants was extended to the end of the 2025/26 financial year with £6.5 million in funding. The maximum grant is £16,000 for small trucks and £25,000 for large trucks.

Policy: Rail development framework plan 2025-2030
Policy_Content: This plan envisages investments of approximately €19.7 billion for the expansion of rail infrastructure from 2025 to 2030.

Policy: Rail from Kemi to Narvik
Policy_Content: The Finnish government allocated €20 million for an initial track gauge study as part of a long-term project to switch to the standard European gauge, starting with a rail connection from Kemi to Narvik.

Policy: Railway electrification project
Policy_Content: Through the use of the EU Recovery and Resilience Fund, Lithuania plans to allocate EUR 52.2 million to railway electrification by 2026.

Policy: Regulation of sustainability requirements and verification of biofuels, liquid bio-energy carriers and fuels produced from biomass
Policy_Content: According to Government Decree 821/2021. (XII. 28.) between 1 January and 31 December 2025 the mandatory blend rate of biofuels is 8.9%, of which the mandatory minimum share of advanced biofuels, biogas is 1% in 2025 and 3.5% in 2030.

Policy: Regulation ЕАEU 048/2019 on requirements for energy efficiency of energy-consuming devices
Policy_Content: The regulation aims to ensure energy efficiency and resource conservation in the framework of the Eurasian Economic Union.It notably sets standards for a number of appliances (e.g. refrigeration appliances, electric equipements) and electric asynchronous motors - equivalent to IE2 requirements.

Policy: Resolution 67/2025 - GBA Storage - AlmaGBA
Policy_Content: Resolution 67/2025 aims at fostering the contracting of electric energy storage plants, with an estimated investment of USD 500 million and an execution period of between 12 and 18 months.

Policy: Rooftop solar subsidy scheme for households
Policy_Content: Private buildings with a roof area of less than 1,000 square meters can receive a subsidy of 3,000 yuan per kilowatt (kW), with a maximum of 300,000 yuan per case, and can be combined with additional subsidies from local governments.

Policy: Saudi Electricity Company Battery Energy Storage Systems Awards
Policy_Content: Saudi Electricity Company (SEC) awards contracts for 2,500 MW Battery Energy Storage Systems across Saudi Arabia.

Policy: Saudi Green Building Code 2024 (SBC 1001)
Type: Building energy codes for new buildings
Policy_Content: The Saudi Building Code is a collection of legislative, administrative, and technical rules for new buildings in Saudi Arabia. The Green Building code is part of it and promotes green practices in the sector over energy efficiency and CO2 emissions reduction.

Policy: Second NDC of Brazil
Policy_Content: Brazil aims to reduce its GHG emissions to 0.85-1.05 Gt CO2eq by 2035.

Policy: Second NDC of Japan
Policy_Content: Japan aims at reducing its GHG emissions by 60% below 2013 levels by 2035, and by 73% by 2040.

Policy: Second NDC of New Zealand
Policy_Content: New Zealand aims at reducing its GHG emissions by 51 to 55% below 2005 levels by 2035.

Policy: Second NDC of Singapore
Policy_Content: Singapore aims at capping emissions at around 45 to 50 MtCO2e by 2035.

Policy: Second NDC of Switzerland
Policy_Content: The Second NDC aims at reducing its GHG emissions by at least 65% below 1990 levels by 2035.

Policy: Second NDC of United Kingdom
Policy_Content: The United Kingdom aims at reducing its GHG emissions by at least 81% below 1990 levels by 2035.

Policy: Service Area Pilot Program with Ultra-Fast Charging Stations
Policy_Content: This programme aims to contribute to the decarbonisation of transport, catalyse private investment in electric charging infrastructures and improve the offer of services to the user. The deployment of the program will be carried out through contracts for the concession of works of new service areas Finally, eight service areas have been planned.

Policy: Signalling of Charging Stations with access from the RCE (Phase 1)
Policy_Content: In the context of adaptation to climate change, decarbonisation and the promotion of sustainable mobility, and with the aim of improving the visibility and accessibility of charging infrastructure for electric vehicles, the DGC has decided to proceed with the ex officio signalling of certain Charging Stations with access from the RCE. Policy: Special Act on National Resource Security
Policy_Content: The Special Act on National Resource Security, promulgated on 6 February 2024 and effective from 7 February 2025, establishes comprehensive measures to prepare for and respond to resource security crises by implementing early warning systems, managing supply and demand of core resources and establishing crisis response mechanisms. The law creates a new framework for resource security governance through several key mechanisms:Resource security has become increasingly important for national security and economic stability. This law addresses growing concerns about supply chain vulnerabilities and the need to secure stable access to critical resources including energy sources, minerals and materials essential for renewable energy technologies. This legislation strengthens South Korea's resource security by establishing systematic crisis prevention and response capabilities. It enables coordinated government action during resource emergencies while promoting long-term resource security through stockpiling requirements, supply chain diversification and development of alternative materials. The law provides legal basis for government intervention in resource markets during crises, potentially affecting business operations but enhancing overall national resource security.

Policy: Standardised energy savings certificate (CEE) operation sheets

These sheets define eligible actions and corresponding energy savings, allowing obligated parties (mainly energy suppliers) to offer financial incentives or “CEE bonuses” to beneficiaries. The new operations include the purchase or long-term lease of new electric vehicles (both light and heavy-duty), as well as electric retrofit operations. These measures are accessible to private individuals, legal entities, and local authorities, and aim to reduce the upfront cost of electric mobility by leveraging the energy savings generated.

Policy: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate

The new codes cover various stages of the battery life cycle, including manufacturing, post-consumer batteries, and intermediate fractions from recycling, ensuring proper handling and boosting battery recycling efforts within the EU.
