Policy: RES – a source of heat for heating
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: Poland's RES – a source of heat for heating program earmarks financial support to support investments in the production of heat from renewable sources.

Policy: RM2 billion in National Energy Transition Roadmap Seed Fund
Policy_Content: The Malaysian government unveiled the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) on 27 July 2023 to facilitate energy transition through the six main pillars - energy efficiency, renewable energy, hydrogen, bioenergy, green mobility and carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS).Phase 1 of the NETR has attracted RM25 billion of investments from public and private sector, with the government committing a total of RM2 billion in terms of seed funding.A non-exhaustive list of projects to be implemented are:- Floating hydro solar power: 2500MW TNB hydro dam reservoir- Residential solar power: Construction of 4.5 MW residential rooftop solar power plants;- Hydrogen: Implementation of three integrated hydrogen production plants in Sarawak- Eco-friendly mobility: 10,000 EV charging stations; electrification of public transport;- Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage (CCUS): Petronas-led catalyst project in the high-CO2 Kasawari and Lang Lebah gas fieldsThe government will complete the final section of NETR in Phase 2 with a comprehensive action plan and initiatives to spur investment and economic activity

Policy: Rare earth elements content disclosure in consumer goods
Policy_Content: The February 10, 2020 law on fighting wastefulness and on the circular economy (n°2020-105) aims to enhance transparency and promote environmentally responsible consumer choices by providing detailed product information. It includes a provision requiring the disclosure of precious metals and rare earths content present in consumer goods. This rule applies to vehicles and electronic goods and will progressively come into force from 2023 to 2025. This legal obligation is codified in article L.541-9-1 of the Environment Code, and implementation rules can be found in section VIII of article R. 541-221 in the same code. It specifies the following: 1. : For certain electrical and electronic equipment, a repairability index (or a durability index from 1 January 2024) is displayed, indicating how easily the product can be repaired.2. : This concept is defined by criteria including effective collection, sorting, absence of elements that impede recycling, and the ability to recycle more than 50% of the material by mass. Products meeting these criteria are labeled as "mostly recyclable" or "entirely recyclable."3. : Products containing more than 1 milligram of gold, silver, platinum, or palladium must be labeled with the quantity of each metal.4. : Similar to precious metals, products containing rare earth elements above a certain threshold must be labeled with the specific quantity.

Policy: Recommended Guideline for Greenhouse Gas and Carbon Intensity Accounting Frameworks for LNG/Hydrogen/Ammonia Projects
Policy_Content: In 2023, the Japan Energy and Metals National Corporation ('JOGMEC') issued the Recommended Guideline for Greenhouse Gas and Carbon Intensity Accounting Frameworks for LNG/Hydrogen/Ammonia Projects (“CI Guideline”). The guideline suggests a transparent method for calculating GHG emissions and CI containing methane, based on multiple existing international standards. For methane emission measurement, the guideline recommends a bottom-up approach (gas sampling, imaging with an infrared camera at the site, etc.) for measurement from individual emission sources, and a top-down approach (using satellites and drones) for measurement from sites or regions.

Policy: Recycle - Change Water Heaters programme
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The programme "Recycle - Change Water Heaters", amounting to EUR 100 million for 2023, aims at reducing electricity consumption by 65% for at least 120,000 households.

Policy: Red Sea Wind Energy - Green Egypt
Policy_Content: The Red Sea Wind Energy Project contributes to Egypt’s green transition with the financial support of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).Launched in 2023, the EBRD’s loan of USD 100 million will allow for the creation of a 500 MW onshore wind farm in the Gulf of Suez region, with USD 50 million provided by the Green Climate Fund and USD 50 million by the EBRD.

Policy: Reduction of wholesale gas price
Policy_Content: The Government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina adopted a decision on reduction of the wholesale price of natural gas by 12.53 percent. Following this decision natural gas distributors can sell natural gas at 0.866 KM/Sm³ as of 1 April 2023.

Policy: Regional Hydrogen Transition
Policy_Content: The Regional Hydrogen Transition is aimed at providing consumer subsidy for early-stage hydrogen adopters in order to support hydrogen producers and industry at large. Specific sectors that will be eligible for consumption subsidies and rebate are:While the final program design is still underway, the New Zealand government has allocated NZD 100 million for the initiative, with a NZD 32.6 million allocated for the first four years.

Policy: Regional Microgrids Program
Policy_Content: In October 2020, the Australian Government announced AUD 2.47 billion in funding for measures that aim to lower energy prices, reduce emissions and boost the economy. As part of this initiative, the Program has been allocated AUD 50 million over six years (2020-21 to 2025-26) to support pilot projects for microgrids in regional Australia.The Program aims to support microgrid projects that:- Have been found to be feasible through a feasibility study or equivalent investigation- Include the deployment of equipment and technology solutions that enable the microgrid demonstration- Demonstrate improved resilience and reliability of microgrids in regional areas- Are capable of resolving remaining barriers to final investment and full deployment.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation
Policy_Content: This regulation establishes binding targets for the deployment of publicly accessible recharging and refueling infrastructure across the EU. It aims to ensure the development of a dense, interoperable, and user-friendly network to support the transition to zero-emission mobility. Starting from 2025, fast charging stations (≥150 kW) must be available every 60 km along the core TEN-T road network for passenger cars, with higher capacity requirements by 2030. For heavy-duty vehicles, charging hubs with a minimum total power output must be deployed every 120 km from 2025 and increase significantly by 2030. The regulation also sets targets for hydrogen refueling stations and mandates clear rules on payment methods, price transparency, and real-time availability of charging points to improve user experience and confidence.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 Use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport
Policy_Content: The regulation aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the shipping sector, by promoting the use of cleaner fuels and energy, promoting the decarbonisation of the maritime transport sector by setting maximum limits on the yearly greenhouse gas intensity of the energy used by a ship (2% reduction in 2025, increasing in 5 year intervals out to 80% reduction in 2050). There will also be a requirement for certain ships to plug into onshore power supply while at berth in certain ports from 2030.

Policy: Regulation Regarding Petroleum Products Specification and Standards for Implementation
Policy_Content: This regulation states updated increase in blending requirement on biofuels. It lists:These rates are effective as of September 2023.

Policy: Regulation for small electrical products and solar photovoltaic systems
Policy_Content: The Australian Government is proposing to implement a national, legislated product stewardship scheme for small electrical and electronic equipment (SEEE) and solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. This initiative comes in response to the growing e-waste problem in Australia, where each person generates around 20kg of e-waste annually, one of the highest per capita rates globally. The proposed regulation aims to address the environmental and health costs associated with e-waste, increase recycling and material recovery rates, and support Australia's transition to a circular economy. The Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water has developed this proposal in consultation with industry stakeholders, recyclers, peak bodies, regulators, and state and territory governments.The regulation would cover small electrical and electronic equipment (SEEE) up to 20kg and solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. The proposal includes the following:Implementation of the regulation will follow existing product stewardship provisions under the Recycling and Waste Reduction Act 2020.

Policy: Regulation on setting the price of electricity for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises

Policy: Renewable Energy Electricity Subsidy for 2023
Policy_Content: The Chinese government earmarked subsidies for renewable electricity generation (wind, solar and biomass) provided to local public utilities and power generation companies in 2023. The initial budget was enacted end 2022, and additionnal funding was earmarked in June 2023.

Policy: Renewable Energy Industry Export Support Plan
Policy_Content: The Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy (MOTIE) announced the Renewable Energy Industry Export Support Plan aimed at supporting domestic renewable energy manufacturers' access to foreign markets.Specific measures include:Other measures with no specific funding announced include:

Policy: Renewable Energy Transformation Agreements (RETAs)
Policy_Content: The Commonwealth Government has been negotiating bilateral Renewable Energy Transformation Agreements (RETAs) with states and territories since late 2023. RETAs build on collaboration through the National Energy Transformation Partnership and support common goals in the energy transition. Through RETAs, governments commit to working together to deliver new renewable generation and storage to support achieving 82% renewable electricity nationally by 2030, including through agreed minimum allocations of capacity for states as part of the Capacity Investment Scheme.

Policy: Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) Program: Standards for 2023–2025
Policy_Content: The Renewable Fuel Standard programme is a national policy that requires a certain volume of renewable fuel to replace or reduce the quantity of petroleum-based transportation fuel, heating oil or jet fuel.In June 2023, the EPA updated the standards to 11.96% of renewable fuels in 2023 // 12.50% in 2024 // 13.13% in 2025.

Policy: Renewable Heat Act - coal and oil heating systems phase-out
Type: Ban of oil boilers;Ban of coal boilers
Policy_Content: The Renewable Heat Act sets milestones for the building sector decarbonisation, including a progressive mandatory decommissioning of coal and oil heating systems.This decommissioning is set to start in 2025, and all coal and oil heating systems are to be shut down by 2035.

Policy: Renewable Heat Act - gas heating system phase-out
Policy_Content: The Renewable Heat Act sets as milestone the decommissioning of gas boilers by 2040, in order to reach Austria's climate neutrality goal by the same date.

Policy: Renewable Transport Fuel Policy 2023-2025
Policy_Content: The updated policy continues to provide a framework for ongoing consultation, analysis and review towards meeting targets set out in the Climate Action Plan 2023 and European obligations for renewable energy supply for use in transport. The policy sets out a pathway to incentivise supply of renewable transport fuel through annual increases in the renewable transport fuel obligation rate to 2030, as well as ensuring European sustainability and greenhouse gas reduction criteria are adhered to.

Policy: Renewable energy and storage deployment - 2023 government spending
Policy_Content: Argentina's National Public Investment Plan (PNIP) allocates resources for the deployment of renewable energy and battery storage

Policy: Resolution 1006 of 30 November 2023
Policy_Content: By way of Resolution 1006 of 2023, the National Mining Agency (ANM) declared the following groups of minerals (and their associated minerals, derivatives or concentrates) as being of strategic interest for Colombia:As per the resolution, the list is to be reviewed and, if necessary, updated within three (3) years. The definition of minerals as strategic responds to guidelines for the mining sector embodied in the National Development Plan 2022-2026 “Colombia World Power of Life” and the guidelines adopted by the Board of Directors of ANM through Agreement No. 01 of 2023. These guidelines are:The resolution repeals Resolution 18 0102 issued on January 30, 2012 by the Ministry of Mines and Energy that set out a list of strategic minerals.

Policy: Resolution 286 on pricing of greenhouse gas emissions
Policy_Content: The government of Israel announced the plan to introduce a carbon tax at slowly increasing level from 2023 to 2028 through a statement approved by the Tax Authority and the Finance, Energy, Environmental Protection and Economy ministries.The nation’s first carbon tax will be applied to coal, liquified petroleum gas, fuel oil, petcoke and gas and is expected to cover about 80% of greenhouse gas emissions by 2028. However, the tax would not be introduced if the electricity price would rise by more than 5% through 2028. Additionally, diesel and gasoline will not be taxed any further as part of the scheme, due to existing levies.At a later stage, the tax will cover the emissions from other sources of global warming gases, such as garbage dumps, responsible for 8% of Israel’s GHG emissions, and cooling gases used in air conditioning systems, refrigerators, and refrigerated vehicles, which account for 7% of GHG emissions.

Policy: Resolution 40715/2019: Wholesale Energy Market with RES in 2023
Policy_Content: To reach a more eco-friendly energy matrix, the Ministry of Mines and Energy approved resolution 40715 that stipulates that, as of 2023, at least 10% of electricity purchases of wholesalers of the Wholesale Energy Market destined to serve end users must come from renewables (FNCER), through long-term contracts.In 2019, this requirement was partially regulated for marketers that serve regulated users, that is, residential, commercial and small industry, with a validity for 2022. From 2023 this measure come to an effect for all end users.

Policy: Resolution 714/2023 - Clean energy technology import tax exemption
Policy_Content: In 2023, the Argentinian government implemented a PAIS tax (Tax for an Inclusive and Solidarity Argentina) import tax exemption for goods used in foreign stakeholders' electricity generation sector activities and projects .

Policy: Resolution No. 3/2023 on the evolution of the mandatory addition of biodiesel to diesel oil sold to the final consumer
Policy_Content: The National Energy Policy Council (CNPE) published in March 2023 new biodiesel blending target, targeting 15% by 2026.It enacted an increase in April 2023 from 10% to 12%, and schedule an increase to 13% by 2024 // 14% by 2025 // 15% by 2026.

Policy: Resolution to adopt a New National Mining Policy
Policy_Content: In August 2022, the Council of the State, within the process of Popular Action 2013-02459-01, ordered the Ministry of Mines and Energy to update the National Mining Policy within 6 months. Thus, in June 2023, the Ministry released the proposal for a new National Mining Policy entitled “A New Vision of Mining in Colombia.” The new policy projects a reorientation of the mining industry to meet the objectives of the National Development Plan 2022-2026, with a view to 2035.The Policy is oriented by six guiding approaches:Furthermore, the Policy identifies 10 problems in the mining industry and proposes a set of strategic measures for each:

Policy: Revised Act on Restriction on Special Cases Concerning Taxation
Type: Government spending in storage;Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The Act on Restriction on Special Case Concerning Taxation provides tax exemptions, reductions, and modifications for specific categories in order to support policy objectives. The Act was revised in 2023 to increase tax credits for national strategic industries including semiconductors, batteries, hydrogen and other advanced vehicle technologies. The revision was referred to as the "K-Chips Act" by some media outlets, as a response to the US CHIPS and Science Act that focuses on boosting domestic semi-conductor investment.Specifically, rates of tax credits provided to facilitate investments in the national strategic industries were raised from 16% to 25% for small- and medium-enterprises; and from 8% to 15% for large-enterprises. The revision also provided an additional 10% in tax credits for investments above the three-year average amount (2020-2023). Finally, a temporary tax credit for general and high-tech investments in the national strategic industries was introduced for 2023.The tax credit benefits provided by the Act is scheduled to conclude at the end of 2024.

Policy: Revised Domestic Gas Pricing
Policy_Content: The natural gas price in India as per the 2014 guidelines is fixed every six months based on the weighted average price of four global benchmarks (Henry Hub, Alberta gas, NBP, and Russian gas). In April 2023, the Indian government approved revisions of the guidelines under the administered price mechanism (APM), which mainly applies to gas produced by legacy fields and national oil companies (ONGC, OIL).Key revisions of the guidelines include:

Policy: Revision of Import Tariff for Glass
Policy_Content: Chinese Taipei decreased its import tariff for quartz glass products used in the semiconductor industry from 10% to 1.2% in 2023.

Policy: Revolving Fund for Energy Efficiency
Policy_Content: The Government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina allocated BAM 4.7 million for 2023 to the Revolving Fund for Energy Efficiency, which finances energy efficiency measures in the public buildings sector through the state-owned Union Banka.

Policy: Roadmap for the development of the oil and gas chemical complex until 2025
Policy_Content: In 2023, the Russian government announced an updated roadmap for the petrochemical industry, aiming at boosting the development of oil and gas chemical clusters in the Arctic zone and the production of base polymers by 34% by 2025.

Policy: Royal Decree 36/2023, of 24 January, establishing a system of Energy Efficiency Certificates
Policy_Content: On 26 January 2023, came into force, the Royal Decree 36/2023, of 24 January, establishing a system of Energy Efficiency Certificates (CAE System in Spain) in development of the provisions of article 71.2 of Spanish Law 18/2014, of 15 October and transposing the European Directive on Energy Efficiency (EED) into national law. The CAE System is a mechanism designed for accrediting the achievement of energy savings with the aim of contributing to the fulfilment, by 2030, of the final energy savings targets set by the EED.The CAE System emerge to facilitate investment in energy efficiency technologies and foster a market in this sector. This system applies to investments in every sector, not only private or public, but also industry, buildings, transport or service sector.

Policy: Royal Decree No. 10/2023
Policy_Content: The Royal Decree No. 10/2023 allocates land for renewable energy and clean hydrogen projects. Since February 2023, the Ministry of Energy and Minerals has the full competency to define and implement the scope of green energy activities and clean hydrogen projects to be implemented on site.

Policy: Rural Clean Energy Initiative & Support to rural energy transition
Policy_Content: The 2023 Budget of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) allocates USD 300 million to support rural electricity providers in the transition to clean energy sources in addition to USD 6.5 billion for rural electric loans. These funds will be used to finance clean energy transition projects, including renewable energy and energy storage expansion, transmission updates, and job creation. Another USD 15 million is provided for the creation of the Rural Clean Energy Initiative to manage efficient use of funding.

Policy: SEK 380 million: Temporary tax reduction on agricultural diesel
Policy_Content: Temporary tax reduction on agricultural diesel

Policy: SEK 6.73 billion: Temporary reduction of tax on petrol and diesel
Policy_Content: The Government of Sweden enacted a reduction of the tax on petrol and diesel by the equivalent of one krona per litre at the refuelling stations as of 2023 to support households and businesses facing high energy costs.

Policy: Safe and sustainable access to innovation-critical raw materials
Policy_Content: The Swedish Foundation for Strategic Environmental Research (Mistra) has released a call for proposals for a research programme for "safe and sustainable access to innovation-critical raw materials". The future research programme will use a strategic environmental perspective to identify risks and opportunities regarding access to metals and minerals deemed critical for a sustainable transition of society. The programme is expected to be cross-disciplinary and focus on the social, economic and environmental challenges across the value chain in society’s future provision of innovation-critical raw materials. Mistra will offer a maximum budget of SEK 20 million over a four-year period. This call for proposals is closely related to that of the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research announced the same year for a .

Policy: Saudi Arabia - Vale-Minerals Agreement
Policy_Content: On July, 2023, Manara Minerals, a joint venture between Ma’aden, a state owned company, and Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, signed a binding agreement with Vale Base Metals Limited (VBM) for an equity interest of 10% at an enterprise implied value of US$26 billion. The partnership will expand VBM's copper and nickel production, and will allow Manara Minerals access to VBM mining projects in Canada, Brazil, and Indonesia. Therefore, Saudi Arabia will secure high purity minerals such as copper, nickel, and lithium, which are essential for the Kingdom's 2030 domestic manufacturing vision of electric vehicles, aluminum, and battery cells.

Policy: Second call for solar power plants
Policy_Content: Luxembourg launched the second call for photovoltaic projects to encourage companies to set up and operate solar plants in Luxembourg for their own electricity consumption. The call is open between 15 July and 31 Oct 2023.

Policy: Shandong Home Appliance Consumption Promotion
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The local government of Shandong has earmarked financial support to promote subsidies for the purchase of consumer home appliances.

Policy: Singapore Economy 2030
Policy_Content: The Singapore Economy 2030 vision has four key pillars of Trade, Enterprise, Manufacturing and Services. It outlines Singapore's strategies to support local enterprises by maximising human capital through various programs, developing innovation capabilities, and ensuring energy security through diversification and international collaborations.

Policy: Solar PV import tariff quota
Policy_Content: From 2024 to 2027, the Brazilian government is implementing a tariff rate quota (TRQ) exempting solar panel imports from border tariff within the quantitative limits set. Imports above quota limits are subject to a 9.6% import tariff.Decreasing quantitative limits are set from 2024 to 2027. From 2028 onwards, solar panels imports are expected to be subject to a 9.6% import tariff.

Policy: Solar PVs on Government Facilities
Policy_Content: The Malaysian government is financing theinstallation of solar panels on government buildings by end 2023.

Policy: Solar Recycling Research & Development program
Policy_Content: Funded by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to award financial assistance to eligible entities for research, development, demonstration, and commercialization projects to create innovative and practical approaches to increase the reuse and recycling of solar energy technologies.

Policy: Solar power project import duty exemption
Policy_Content: In 2023, the government of Panama enacted an incentive regime for solar power plants and installations, including an import duty exemption for related equipment, machinery, materials, and items necessary for the construction, operation, and maintenance of such activities.

Policy: Solar rooftop installation in Istanbul
Policy_Content: The Turkish government allocated funding in to install 11.84MW of rooftop solar power plant in Istanbul. The project is expected to be completed by 2026.

Policy: Southeast Asia METEC (The Methane Emissions Technology Evaluation Center)
Policy_Content: In June 2023, JOGMEC and Malaysia’s national oil and gas company (PETRONAS) announced the establishment of a methane emissions technology evaluation center (METEC) to promote cooperation for mitigating methane emissions in the ASEAN region. The facility is set to provide support to companies in studying the MMRV processes for methane emissions, assisting in the reduction of methane emissions in the ASEAN region, and supporting implementation plans for methane measurement technology.

Policy: Special Act on National Strategic Technology Development
Policy_Content: The Special Act on National Strategic Technology Development commits the government to formulating a five-year master plan for fostering and protecting national strategic technologies. This plan includes annual detailed implementation plans for each strategic technology field. Strategic technologies are identified and managed through consultations with relevant administrative agencies and deliberations by the designated Science and Technology Advisory Council. The development of these technologies will be supported by designated agencies and research institutions, the creation of regional technology innovation hubs to foster a research ecosystem, linking industries, and operating specialized educational institutions.

Policy: Special Funds for Demonstration Application of Fuel Cell Vehicles in Shanghai
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: Shanghai Municipal Economic and Information Technology Commission has announced a special fund to encourage technological innovation and demonstration applications in fuel cell vehicles. It came into effect in April 2023 and will end in December 2025. This fund is a combination of central and local government's fund. The fund supportsVehicle demonstration application. If fuel cell vehicles meet the relevant requirements of both the country and this city for demonstration applications, and have obtained national comprehensive assessment reward points, Shanghai will award CNY 200 thousand per reward point. Vehicle operation. Operation rewards will be given to fuel cell trucks and commercial commuter buses that have a mileage of more than 20,000 kilometers in each assessment year. Each vehicle will be rewarded for a maximum of 3 years from the time it obtains the operating quota. Among them, trucks with a total design mass of 12-31 tons (inclusive) will be rewarded CNY 5 thousand per vehicle per year, heavy trucks with a total design mass exceeding 31 tons will be rewarded CNY 20 thousand per vehicle per year, and commuter buses will be rewarded CNY 10 thousand per vehicle per year. Industrialization of key components. Key parts and components that meet the relevant requirements of Shanghai are used in vehicle applications in domestic demonstration city clusters. Points will be awarded based on the national comprehensive assessment. The relevant district will award bonus funds to the enterprise based on the points gained. In principle, CNY 30 thousand will be awarded for each point. The total amount of rewards for similar key parts products of each enterprise shall not exceed CNY 30 million.Demonstration application of fuel cell buses. Vehicle purchase and operation subsidy standards are implemented in accordance with the city’s new energy bus development support policies.Layout and construction of fuel cell vehicle hydrogenation stations. If building a fuel cell hydrogenation station within this city in accordance with relevant regulations, complete completion acceptance and obtain a gas operation license and a gas supply site license, Shanghai will provide support based on no more than 30% of the total approved investment in equipment purchase and installation. Operation of fuel cell vehicle hydrogenation stations. For hydrogenation stations that have obtained a gas business license and a gas supply site license, if the retail price of hydrogen does not exceed 35 CNY/kg, support is provided based on actual annual hydrogen sales.

Policy: Standards B.E. 2566 for controlling air emissions from power plants
Policy_Content: Thailand updated its air pollutant emissions standards in 2023, with applicable norms depending on the age of the installation and its fuel.Air emission standards for new power plants are as follows:For power plants licensed to operate before 1996, limits for SO2 are 60-320 mg / m3 // NOx to 200-500 mg / m3 // PM to 120-180 mg / m3For power plants licensed to operate between 1996 and 2010, limits for SO2 are 20-640 mg / m3 // NOx to 120-350 mg / m3 // PM to 60-120 mg / m3For power plants licensed to operate between 2010 and 2023, limits for SO2 are 20-360 mg / m3 // NOx to 120-200 mg / m3 // PM to 60-120 mg / m3

Policy: State aid for energy costs of energy intensive sectors
Policy_Content: The Polish Government allocated PLN 5 billion in state aid for energy intensive industrial companies to help cover the increases in natural gas and electricity costs incurred in 2022. The aid is disbursed by the Ministry of Development and Technology from February 2023 to eligible undertakings with annual electricity consumption of more than 20 TWh, whose electricity or gas prices have increased by 50% compared to the average price in 2021.The amount of support covers up to 50% of eligible costs incurred from February to December 2022, in the maximum amount of EUR 4 million per undertaking. In case the undertaking had a decrease in earnings of at least 40% between 2021 and 2022 or had negative earnings, the amount is increased to 80% of eligible costs and up to EUR 50 million per undertaking.

Policy: State loan to cover energy prices
Policy_Content: The state export bank Eximbanka of Slovakia provides loans to companies with minimum of 20% revenues from export to cover high electricity and natural gas costs. The loan amount will be defined on a case-by-case basis and there is no particular budget allocation.

Policy: Statement on Seabed Mining
Policy_Content: Natural Resources Canada released a statement in 2023 regarding the country's official position on seabed mining. The statement reaffirms Canada's commitment to increasing the percentage of protected marine and coastal areas in its territory to 25% in 2025 and 30% in 2030. is regulated by federal legislation that includes the Oceans Act, Species at Risk Act and Fisheries Act. The prohibits industrial activities including mining, oil and gas exploration and exploitation, waste disposal and bottom trawling in federally protected marine areas that were established after April 25, 2019. Exemptions from the standard apply to activities conducted for the following reasons: 1) public and vessel safety, 2) national defence, 3) national security, 4) law enforcement, 5) responding to an emergency, 6) aboriginal and treaty rights, 7) adherence with international law, 8) any other matter the Minister deems necessary for the implementation of the Standard. There is currently no domestic legal framework that would permit seabed mining in Canada, and the Statement affirms that Canada will not authorise this activity without the implementation of a rigorous regulatory structure that incorporates due diligence, precautionary and ecosystem-based approaches and engagement with the public, including with Indigenous Peoples. With regard to , the Statement reaffirms Canada's position that knowledge about the impacts of deep-sea mining and adoption of robust environmental standards by the International Seabed Authority is a necessary precursor to the authorisation of this activity.

Policy: Stimulation of Sustainable Energy Production and Climate Transition (SDE++)
Type: Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending in biofuels
Policy_Content: Launched on September 2023, the SDE+ focuses on the options of renewable electricity, renewable gas and renewable heat and subsidises, the difference between the cost price of renewable energy and the market price, to encourage the deployment of renewables in the Netherlands.

Policy: Strategic plan to protect country's infrastructure
Policy_Content: The Plan aims at setting standards and requirements for high-value infrastructures, including the energy and transportation sectors.

Policy: Strategy for Industrial New Growth through Invigoration of Circular Economy
Policy_Content: The Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) announced the strategy for the swift spread of circular economy across all industries to support private sector’s shift towards carbon neutrality and efforts to develop new sources of competitiveness as well as to secure an internal supply chain for core resources. MOTIE aims to upgrade the national integrated resources management system (k-mfa.kr), establish a certification system, and uncover firms that hold promising potential for circular economy.The strategy consists of nine circular economy projects assigned to nine major industries titled “Project CE (Circular Economy) 9” which includes:1. Expanding the production of pyrolysis oil2. Transition to high-quality materials3. Maximising the utilisation of steel scraps4. Recycling rare metals5. Establishing the basis for recycling and reusing of battery6. Accelerating the production and use of renewable materials7. Introducing and implementing eco-design8. Boosting exports of remanufactured products9. Securing alternative sources of fuel materialsThis will entail organising and managing a consultative body composed of relevant ministries to facilitate discussions on measures for the utilisation of production process by-products and support the establishment of internal and external supply chain of renewable materials.

Policy: Strategy for Sustainable Mining in Andalusia 2030
Policy_Content: The Strategy for Sustainable Mining in Andalusia 2030 (EMSA 2030) is a comprehensive economic development framework approved in July 2023 that aims to transform Andalusia's mining sector through environmental, economic, and social sustainability measures through 2030.The strategy is structured around seven thematic blocks, including situation analysis, governance principles, foundational bases, fundamental components (mission, vision, and objectives), action lines, planning instruments, and governance principles. It establishes eleven strategic objectives, focusing on territorial value creation, innovation enhancement, mineral resource transformation, critical raw materials supply to European markets, development of mining services companies, energy efficiency improvements, carbon footprint reduction, worker safety enhancement, employment quality improvement, administrative simplification, and environmental impact reduction. The implementation is planned across two periods: 2023-2026 and 2027-2030.This framework aims to position Andalusia as a reference point for sustainability in mining whilst supporting regional development. The strategy seeks to create quality employment, strengthen territorial cohesion, and align with European, Spanish, and Andalusian industrial policies. Through its implementation, the programme intends to balance economic development with environmental protection, contributing to the region's 'green revolution' whilst ensuring the mining sector's long-term viability.

Policy: Strategy for the Development of Industrial Parks until 2030
Policy_Content: The strategy for the development of industrial parks until 2030 aims at:- Improving the legal framework for the creation, operation and development of industrial parks,- Optimising and developing the network of industrial parks, taking into account the priorities and needs of business, communities and the state – current and prospective.- Strengthening cooperation with relevant international, governmental and non-governmental organisations, national and foreign partners in ensuring the functioning of industrial parks and attracting investments;- Promoting the formation and application of industrial park management practices that correspond to the best global approaches.

Policy: Subsidies for Electricity Bills 2023
Policy_Content: Starting from January to April 2023, the Thai government earmarked THB 75 billion for electricity subsidies to soften the impact of energy prices. Discounts for electricity bills will be allocated to households that consume a maximum of 300 units of electricity per month and reside in the areas covered by the services provided under the concessions contract of the Royal Thai.The subsidies are distributed by the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA) and the Metropolitan Electricity Administration (MEA).

Policy: Subsidy for Czech electricity TSO ČEPS
Policy_Content: The Czech Ministry of Industry and Trade will provide a subsidy of CZK 22.7 billion to the Czech electricity transmission system operator ČEPS to cover increased costs of electricity procured to cover energy losses in the transmission system and for ensuring system services. The subsidy aims at shielding final consumers from an increase in electricity transmission costs.

Policy: Subsidy for heat producers
Policy_Content: The Czech Ministry of Industry and Trade announced to provide in 2023 subsidies to heat producers to cover higher costs of heat generation. The aim is to shield customers from high prices since the subsidy beneficiary will be obliged to decrease heat prices accordingly.

Policy: Subsidy for household energy bills
Policy_Content: The Romanian Ministry of European Investments and Projects provides a one-time subsidy of RON 1,400 to 4 million vulnerable households to compensate for rising energy prices. The subsidy can be used in two instalments between February and December 2023 via a special card.

Policy: Subsidy scheme encouraging the purchase of electric buses and electric heavy weight trucks by transport companies
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: France introduced a subsidy scheme meant to support the purchase of electric heavy weight trucks, busses and corresponding charging infrastructures by transport companies. Two calls for projects were launched in 2023.

Policy: Subsidy scheme to develop cogeneration from municipal biogas
Policy_Content: The Polish Ministry of Climate and Environment, the Consultative Council of the Modernization Fund and the European Investment Bank approved a subsidy programme with a total allocation of PLN 1.5 billion to co-finance the development of cogeneration with municipal biogas in the form of grant or loans covering 50% or 100% of eligible costs respectively. The programme supports the construction of new, extension or modernization of existing installations for the fermentation of municipal organic waste and the use of the obtained biogas to generate energy through high-efficiency cogeneration. The programme receives applications from companies from February to June 2024 and covers eligible costs for the period from September 2022 to December 2030.

Policy: Sunnylands Statement on Enhancing Cooperation to Address the Climate Crisis
Policy_Content: The Sunnylands Statement on Enhancing Co-operation to Address the Climate Crisis, released in advance of COP 28, reaffirms the commitment of the United States and China to work jointly and with other countries to address the climate crisis.Among other climate commitments, the countries agreed upon a number of actions specifically targeting reductions in methane and other non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions:

Policy: Support Program for the Technological Development of the Semiconductor Industry (PADIS)
Policy_Content: Brazil' Semiconductor Industry Technological Development Support Program (PADIS) provides tax incentives to domestic manufacturers of semiconductor equipment used in the solar energy industry.

Policy: Support Scheme for Renewable Heat - Expanded grants
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications and the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland (SEAI) announced in 2023 the expansion of its Support Scheme for Renewable Heat (SSRH).The following changes will be implemented in the scheme, subject to final State aid approval:

Policy: Support for biogas production in Goiás
Policy_Content: The National Bank for Economic and Social Development (BNDES) of Brazil grants additional financing to the company Albioma Codora Energia to implement a biogas production line at the Goianésia/GO cogeneration plant using vinasse from the sugarcane fermentation.

Policy: Support for decarbonising the economy
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The Renovation Campaign offers national funding für households to insulate their buildings to reduce energy and replace fossil heating systems to decarbonise the room heating in Austria. With the financial package of the 2023-2025 budget in Austria about 224.000 projects had been registered with a funding budget of 3,65 billion Euro, more than 130.000 had been implemented until end of 2024. with the aim to support the decarbonisation of room heating in its economy until 2040. New money will be allocated for a funding period from 2026 to 2030 after fixing the national budget.

Policy: Support for domestic green hydrogen production
Policy_Content: The Estonian Ministry of Economy allocates up to EUR 49.1 million in subsidies to invest in the creation of green hydrogen value chains - from production to consumption in the transport sector or chemical industry. The support is open to companies registered in Estonia, which can draw up to EUR 20 million and is administered by the Center for Environmental Investments (KIK).

Policy: Support for energy intensive SMEs extended to 2023
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The Energy Cost and Investment Support Program for Manufacturing SMEs launched by the Government of Hungary in October 2022 was extended also to the first quarter of 2023. With a total budget of HUF 120 billion, the program covers up to 50% of energy cost increase or 15% of investment in energy efficiency of energy-intensive SMEs. The eligibility criteria of the total amount of energy costs was lowered to 2% of sales of the applying company and the support was extended also to energy-intensive companies in the tourism sector.

Policy: Support for households affected by energy poverty – MINI House Renovation
Policy_Content: A subsidy scheme financed from the Modernization Fund and intended for increasing energy efficiency and reducing greenhouse gas emissions in low-income households in the Slovak Republic. It is expected that this scheme will support at least 16,940 applications aimed at partial renovation of family houses with the aim of increasing their energy efficiency and reducing greenhouse gas emissions in low-income households and pensioners in the Slovak Republic, with an expected positive impact on air quality in problem regions of the Slovak Republic.

Policy: Support for investment in EV parts manufacturing plant
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The Government of Hungary will provide 5.6 billion forint (EUR 14.3 million) incentive to Boysen Group company that is investing 60 billion forint in a new manufacturing plant producing parts for electric vehicles that will create 400 new jobs.

Policy: Support for the development of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) -Scheme for Viability Gap Funding (VGF)
Policy_Content: I September 2023, the Indian Ministry of Power earmarked funding for a project grant scheme supporting the development of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The scheme will provide viability gap funding for BESS projects up to a total of 40% of capital costs, by 2030-31. The Indian government aims to invest in the development of up to a capacity of 4000 MWh.

Policy: Support for the security of supply of industrial companies
Policy_Content: The Estonian Ministry of Economy and Infrastructure allocated EUR 20 million to manufacturing companies to subsidise the purchase of equipment for the improvement of the security of energy supply such as generators, storage or connection to district heating.The subsidy amount ranges from EUR 10 000 to 200 000 for micro and small enterprises, and up to EUR 500 000 for medium and large companies.The conditions of the support are to be confirmed and the subsidies will be paid out by Enterprise Estonia (EAS) and Kredex.

Policy: Support for the use of storage facilities and other equipment for grid stabilisation purposes
Policy_Content: The purpose of the program is to support activities aimed at improving the power quality parameters of the distribution and distribution network in the country. Including adapting it to the requirements associated with the rapid development of renewable energy sources and vehicle charging points, resulting from the implementation of the priority programs My Current and My Electrician.

Policy: Support programme for the use of renewable energy sources in households
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The Latvian government has developed a support program to help citizens cope with increased energy prices and promote energy independence. The program includes transitioning from fossil fuel heating systems to renewable energy systems like biomass pellet boilers, solar collectors, and heat pumps. It also supports the purchase of renewable energy equipment for electricity production, such as solar panels and wind generators, and the creation of connections to district heating systems. The program is financed by the Auctioning Instrument of Emission Allowances and managed by the Environmental Investment Fund.

Policy: Support scheme to rail transport operators
Policy_Content: Germany announced a support scheme of EUR 1.1 billion to support freight and passenger railway operators using electric traction. The scheme was introduced in the context of soaring energy prices to alleviate the increasing costs of electricity experienced by railway operators, while also aiming to reduce carbon emissions of the transport sector by promoting the electrification. The support scheme will be delivered in the form of a monthly reduction in electricity bills for rail transport operators and it will be cover electricity consumption in the year 2023.

Policy: Support scheme- Appliance upgrade
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: Since 2023, the government of Chinese Taipei is implementing a NT$3000 subsidy for households upgrading air conditioning and refrigerators to tier 1 efficiency standards. In 2024, gas boiler upgrades were incorporated into the scheme.

Policy: Support scheme- Commercial service industry energy efficient upgrade
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: In 2023, the Government of Chinese Taipei introduced a subsidy scheme supporting the upgrade of electrical and air-conditioning appliance in the commercial and service industry.

Policy: Support to electric vehicle procurement and charging infrastructure development
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The Federal Ministry for Digital and Transport Affairs (BMDV) is investing in the procurement of vehicles and the development of charging infrastructure as part of the electric mobility funding guideline via funding calls. Policy: Supporting Australian Critical Minerals
Policy_Content: The Australian government catered for AUD$80.5 million in the 2023-2024 budget to support the development of critical minerals sector, which includes supply chains, international investment, and net zero transition. Policy: Swedish center for strategic metals and minerals
Policy_Content: The Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research (SSF) announced a national call for proposals for the establishment of a Multidisciplinary Research Centre (MRC) to secure the availability of strategic raw materials, MRC-MetMin. Over six years, the centre will conduct scientific and technological development surrounding the exploration, extraction and enrichment of innovation-critical metals. This applies to metals and minerals that are necessary for green/smart transition, rare, of insufficient supply or should not be traded from conflict zones; the call stipulates that the scope includes, but is not limited to, the EU's 2020 List of Critical Raw Materials. Research must be linked to exploration and/or process development; for example: geology, ore genetics, materials science, hydro- and pyrometallurgical process studies, separation and refining techniques, less toxic processing and new metallurgical processes to enable future metal recovery from complex products and material flows (such as mine tailings). A budget of 60 million SEK will be granted to the selected proposal for the six year period.

Policy: System Stability Roadmap
Policy_Content: The System Stability Roadmap provides a roadmap for achieving a secure and robust operation of the power supply system with 100% renewable energy sources. The system stability roadmap was developed by the BMWK with the participation of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA), transmission and distribution system operators, manufacturers, associations, standardization bodies and the scientific community and was adopted by the Federal Government in December 2023.The System Stability Roadmap identifies all processes and process enhancements that are relevant to system stability and shows which actors have to be involved for the implementation. The System Stability Forum under the leadership of the BMWK will accompany and coordinate the implementation process. The BNetzA will monitor the status of the implementation of the identified measures. The System Stability Report, that the transmission system operators have to prepare every two years from 2025 onwards, is an integral part of the monitoring concept.

Policy_Content: The Mobility Orientation Act stipulates that the maximum amount covered by the Tariff for use of the public electricity network (TURPE) is set at 75% for requests for connection to the electricity network submitted to the project owner before December 31, 2025, for the connection of public electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle charging infrastructure installed in service areas on expressways and motorways. A decree of May 12, 2020 provides for such a reduction in connection costs for IRVEs and extends the deadline to December 31, 2025 for service areas on expressways and motorways. Another decree of February 6, 2023 increases this reduction in connection costs to 75% until the end of 2025 for IRVEs included in a validated charging infrastructure master plan (SDIRVE).

Policy: USD 750 million for clean hydrogen technologies
Policy_Content: In March 2023, the U.S. Department of Energy earmarked USD 750 million for research, development, and demonstration activities aiming at reducing the cost of hydrogen produced through electrolysis. Policy: USPTO Climate Change Mitigation Pilot Program
Policy_Content: The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) has launched the Climate Change Mitigation Pilot Program, which prioritizes the processing of patent applications related to technologies that reduce, remove, prevent, and/or monitor greenhouse gas emissions. This program aims to expedite the innovation process for climate change mitigation technologies. Policy_Content: The strategic partnership between the European Union and Zambia aims to secure strategic and critical raw materials in a sustainable manner for the green transition. Policy: [UNDER NEGOTIATIONS] Indonesia-Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) Free Trade Agreements

Policy: Incentive for sustainable biomethane
Policy_Content: The Ministerial Decree of 15 September 2022 aims to promote the incentives for biomethane fed into the natural gas network through capital support (equal to a maximum of 40% of the expenses incurred) and an energy account incentive (incentive tariff applied to the net production of biomethane). Policy: Law on ensuring coal access and price stabilisation
Policy_Content: In June 2022, the Polish government enacted a law aimed at stabilizing coal prices and increasing this resource availability to individual consumers.The regulation, which is implemented in response to the global energy crisis, aims at increasing the coal supply in the country and thus induce price reductions.It defines a guaranteed price for coal and compensation for authorized intermediaries. The price is set at PLN 996.60 gross per 3 tonnes of coal per household. Compensation for authorized brokers will amount to PLN 1 073 / tonne. Entities that decide to cooperate in the program will be required to register, which is expected to guarantee that coal will be transferred to individual recipients at the price indicated in the law.In addition, households have the opportunity to apply for a coal affordability support allowance.

Policy: "Critical metals" call for projects

Projects are expected to be ambitious initiatives that can be rapidly industrialised in France, either by emerging players with the potential to become world-class competitors, or by existing players with an excellent track record.Projects should focus on the production of primary and recycled metals, the development of methods, technologies and processes to digitise and automate the production of raw materials or on the use of metals, to reduce dependence on metals by focusing on specific consumption, volumes required, sufficient qualities and possible substitutions for the same function supplied to the customer.Five selected companies have already been announced, covering lithium extraction, refining, battery and electric devices recycling.
