The grant can cover up to 50% of qualifying costs such as equipment and materials, professional Services orIT services.The grant set a maximum cap at $250,000 per energy-intensive facility and $125,000 per facility for other facilities. The cost of instruments and metering are also not supported for new ventures.

Policy: Enhancement of NGV conversion programme
Policy_Content: In the context of the global energy crisis, the government of Peru increased the budget and geographical of its NGV conversion programme, which provides a PEN 1000 support by vehicle conversion. A first enhancement took place in April 2022, and a second one was announced in September 2022.The Programme, originally launched in 2021, has to date financed the conversion of 53,200 lightweight vehicles, over 70% of which in the sole year 2022. The Peruvian government specifically promoted the conversion process as a way to lessen the effects of fuel price rise.

Policy: Environmental approval for Hunter Power project (gas-fired power plant)
Policy_Content: The Hunger Power Project's environmental standards, approved by the Australian government, will begin its 660 MW gas-fired power plant at Kurri Kurri with AUD 600 million in government funding. The project will secure affordable, reliable power and create 600 direct jobs and 1,200 indirect jobs. The Hunter Power Project also supports the objectives of the government’s gas-fired recovery program, which is crucial to recover the economy from the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.

Policy: Environmental regulations RE2020 - gas boiler installation ban
Policy_Content: The environmental regulations RE2020 set new norms to the construction sector. It includes the ban of gas heating systems in new houses as of 1st January 2022. It does not cover other buildings.

Policy: Estbdal Initiative
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The Estbdal Initiative provides incentives for the replacement of old window air conditioners with new, more efficient ones, of up to SAR 1,000 for each device.

Policy: European Union Methane Action Plan
Policy_Content: Submitted to the Climate & Clean Air Coalition (CCAC), the EU's Methane Action Plan outlines policies and activities that will support the Global Methane Pledge (GMP) to reduce global emissions by 30% by 2030. The EU's long-term policy goal is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions towards climate neutrality by 2050.Section 1 of the Plan describes the sources and trends in EU's methane emissions. Data in this section comes from EU greenhouse gas inventories. The agriculture sector represents 54% of methane emissions — the largest source of methane emissions in the EU. Emissions in this sector have been reduced by 21% compared to 1990 levels. The energy sector has the smallest contribution of 17% of methane emissions in the EU due to mitigation efforts in the fuel industry contributing a 60% reduction. The waste management sector is also mentioned, representing 27% of methane emissions and a 37% reduction.Section 2 it describes existing EU policies that have contributed to reduction, a review of these policies and additional policies to achieve higher methane emission reductions. Existing policies include:The Plan lists the following policies specific to each sector:Section 3 describes the impact of increased climate ambition, which has historically been reduced steadily since 1990 — 36% in total.Section 4 describes how the EU intends to Monitor and Report on its progress on reducing methane emissions, as well as on the policies and measures that directly impact sectoral methane emissions.

Policy: European Union and Azerbaijan MoU to increase energy cooperation
Policy_Content: On 18 July 2022, the European Union and Azerbaijan signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on a strategic partnership in the field of energy, which includes the commitment to double the capacity of the Southern Corridor pipeline to over 20 bcm a year to the EU by 2027.In the shorter term, Azerbaijan is already increasing its deliveries to the EU, expected at 12 bcm in 2022 compared to 8.1 bcm in 2021.The MoU includes support from the EU to reduce methane flaring and venting in Azerbaijan’s gas production, with the aim to support Azerbaijan's accession to the Global Methane Pledge.

Policy: Exceptional provision of capital to Petroperú
Policy_Content: In October 2022, the Peruvian government proceeded to an exceptional provision of capital to Petroperú, worth in total PEN 4 billion, as well as a PEN 500 million loan guarantee.Both support is meant to ensure the state state-owned company's capacity to maintain domestic supply in petroleum products-notably through imports- in the global energy crisis context.

Policy: Exceptional regime allowing certain gas consumers to return to regulated tariffs
Policy_Content: In an effort to protect domestic consumers from the effects of the global energy crisis, the Portuguese government enacted in September 2022 a temporary and exceptional regime allowing final gas customers with annual consumption less than 10,000 m3 to return to the regulated tariff regime for the sale of natural gas, whose gradual phase out had been decided in 2011. This measure translates into a loss of VAT revenues for the Portuguese State.

Policy: Excise tax reduction of diesel and petrol
Policy_Content: Temporary reduction of 7.5 cents/€ per litre (incl. tax) of Diesel and Petrol, starting from 1st April 2022.

Policy: Executive Action to Spur Domestic Clean Energy Manufacturing by Invoking the Defense Production Act
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: In June 2022, President Biden issued a series of memoranda (Presidential Determinations 2022-15 through 2022-19) invoking the Defense Production Act of 1950 to spur domestic clean energy manufacturing and clean energy projects. These instruct the Department of Energy to take necessary action to rapid expand domestic manufacturing needs, specifically for:Solar panels and parts including modules and module components (Presidential Determination 2022-15);As of May 2024, two funding opportunities have been opened for domestic heat pump manufacturers.

Policy: Exemption of import duties for clean cooking stoves
Policy_Content: Cleaning cooking stoves are exempted from import VAT.

Policy: Exemption of natural gas network costs (charges+taxes) for all residential customers.
Policy_Content: Government to cover natural gas network costs (charges+taxes) for all residential customers, as implemented on 27 April 2022.

Policy: Expansion of FDI Screening regime
Policy_Content: Slovak Republic's law on Screening of Foreign Direct Investments was updated in November 2022. The amendment expanded the scope of FDI screening regime established by the Act No. 45 on critical infrastructure. As part of the new regime, all foreign investments may be screened when there is a reasonable presumption that they may threaten or disrupt security or public order. In addition, foreign investments falling under the category of critical investments should be made only after the approval of the Slovak Ministry of Economy.

Policy: Exploration Strategy for the Mining Industry of South Africa
Policy_Content: The Exploration Strategy for the Mining Industry of South Africa is a strategic plan aimed at attracting mineral exploration investment, reigniting mineral development, accelerating new mineral discoveries and encouraging optimal utilisation of South African mineral resources in line with the environmental, social, and corporate governance principles for sustainable growth.The plan includes a specific provision for the streamlining of regulatory requirements across licensing departments to improve turnaround time on the processing of prospecting rights.The plan also provides a “targeted critical minerals and metals” list categorised by current or future needs.

Policy: Extending the VAT relief available for the installation of energy saving materials (ESMs)
Policy_Content: To help households improve energy efficiency and keep energy costs down – as well as supporting the country's long-term Net Zero ambitions – the UK government is extending the VAT relief available for the installation of energy saving materials (ESMs), from April 2022.The Value Added Tax (Installation of Energy-Saving Materials) Order 2022 amendments are:

Policy: Extension of electricity and gas price caps until August 2023
Policy_Content: The Romanian Government extended the electricity and natural gas price caps from 1 September 2022 until 31 August 2023. For electricity consumers the following price caps apply - RON 0.68/kWh for consumption of 0-100 KWh, RON 0.80/kWh for consumption of 100.01-255 KWh. For natural gas consumers the maximum price is RON 0.31/kWh without a consumption ceiling. Additionally, electricity suppliers are obliged to purchase electricity at a maximum price of RON 1,300 per MW. Natural gas producers can sell gas to suppliers of domestic consumers at maximum of RON 150 per MW.

Policy: Extension of electricity price ceiling of BGN 250/MWh
Policy_Content: The Bulgarian Government extended the compensation mechanism for non-residential electricity consumers and electricity transmission (TSO) and distribution network operators (DSO) for the period of 1 October to 31 December 2022. Under the mechanism all non-residential electricity consumers will be compensated for the difference between the average monthly spot price for base load of the "day-ahead" segment of the Bulgarian Independent Electricity Exchange (IBEX) for the relevant month and the ceiling price of BGN 250/MWh. Approximately 633,000 users will benefit from the compensation.The maximum amount of compensation for the network operators is calculated as the difference between the average monthly base load price of the "day-ahead" segment of IBEX and the estimated market price determined of BGN 421.08/MWh for the TSO and BGN 446.78/MWh for the DSO.

Policy: Extension of the carbon tax suspension
Policy_Content: As part of its March 2022 "New measures to offset rising energy prices" enacted in response to the global energy crisis, the Portuguese government extended the suspension of the carbon tax increase on fuels, set to expire on 31 March 2022, until 30 June 2022. A quarterly revision is then planned until the end of the year. The decision results in a EUR 0.05/L. effective reduction in fuel prices.In July 2022, the suspension was further extended to Q4 2022.

Policy: Families First Price Rise Response Program
Policy_Content: In response to the global energy price crisis, the Portuguese government enacted a EUR 2.4 billion package of household-oriented support measures, of which EUR 612 million are aimed at cushioning rising energy prices by:

Policy: Faster and Further: Canada’s Methane Strategy
Policy_Content: In line with Canada's 2030 Emissions Reduction Plan, Canada issued a Methane Strategy in September 2022 outlining reduction measures and supporting programs to reduce domestic methane emissions by more than 35% by 2030, compared to 2020.The strategy covers federal efforts to: (1) improve monitoring and reporting of methane emissions from the three main emitting sectors (oil and gas, agriculture, and waste); (2) mitigation actions for methane sources from oil and gas, landfills, agriculture, coal mining, buildings, and transportation; (3) create economic opportunities in the methane technology sector; (4) support early, ambitious and sustained international action to rapidly reduce global methane emissions and meet the Global Methane Pledge; (5) sustainably manage natural sources and sinks, for example, through protecting marine and coastal areas.The strategy references emissions reductions targets for each sector, including a 75% reduction in methane emissions from oil and gas operations from 2012 levels by 2030. Key mitigation actions for this are: the federal methane regulations published in 2018; the Emissions Reduction Fund created to invest in green technologies to lower or eliminate methane and other GHG emissions from the oil and gas sector; and strengthened methane regulations to be published in 2023.To reduce methane emissions from coal mines, the strategy outlines the following actions: phasing out unabated coal-fired electricity in Canada by 2030; leading a global effort to phase-out coal-powered electricity; and banning thermal coal exports from Canada by 2030.

Policy: Federal law on subsidiary financial assistance for the rescue of system-critical companies in the electricity industry (FiREG)
Policy_Content: The FiREG is a Federal rescue mechanism for systemically important electricity companies. This rescue mechanism is intended to cover the liquidity needs of electricity companies active in the energy business in the event of extreme price increases or major partner failures.Of the total available credit line of CHF 10 billion to 2026, CHF 4 billion has been drawn by Axpo Holdings. In accordance with the necessity ordinance (and the law currently being examined by Parliament), a lump sum of CHF 15-20 million francs per year applies from the moment the rescue mechanism is activated.

Policy: Final List of Critical Minerals 2022
Policy_Content: As per the Energy Act of 2020, Section 7002, subsection 2, the critical minerals list is revised every three years by the US Geological Survey. The most recent final list is that of 2022.These minerals are deemed critical minerals by the US government in light of their role in national security or economic development. There must be a clear supply chain strategy as they are mostly imported and are, under the US definition, prone to supply chain disruption. Additionally, fuel minerals are excluded from the list of critical minerals.Under the 2022 list, there are 50 minerals which are deemed critical:Note that the bolded items were newly added in 2022 and the items with an asterisk were edited.Modifications from the previous list include:

Policy: Fuel Economy Law (Emergency) 5782
Type: Gas stockholding obligation;Oil stockholding obligation;Oil emergency plan
Policy_Content: The purpose of this law is to maintain emergency stocks of fuels, notably petroleum and gas products. The emergency stock will be purchased by fuel companies.

Policy: Fuel pass I & II
Policy_Content: In an effort to shield domestic consumers from the effects of the global energy crisis, the Greek government implemented in May 2022 a subsidy scheme for transport fuel (petrol and diesel).Individuals and independent workers will benefit from it, depending on their type of vehicle and place of residence.The scheme was extended in July for 3 additional months.

Policy: Fuel subsidies for motor vehicle users
Policy_Content: In July 2022, the Government of Bulgaria approved a budget of BGN 150 million for fuel subsidies. In November 2022, the government allocated an additional budget of BGN 38 million. Under the compensation program, individual users of motor vehicles registered in Bulgaria receive a subsidy of BGN 0.25 per litre of fuel when refueling at gas stations until the end of 2022.

Policy: Funding to promote green heating and phasing down the use of natural gas
Policy_Content: The Danish government has decided to allocate DKK 250 million in 2022 to promote green heating and phasing down the use of natural gas in Denmark, reducing reliance on Russian gas in the process. This includes:

Policy: GB 21454-2021 standard on minimum allowable values of the energy efficiency and energy efficiency grades for multi-connected air-condition (heat pump) units
Policy_Content: The standard sets updated minimum energy performance standards for central air conditioning, with revised grades comparable to Japan or US standards.In January 2024, the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) revised the MEPS, expanding their coverage and setting higher 'Energy Saving' and 'Advanced' levels of equipment across 43 products, 8 of which are cooling products.

Policy: GB 55015-2021 - General Code for Building Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy Utilization
Type: Building energy codes for new buildings
Policy_Content: The code implemented in April 2022 requires that all new, expanded and reconstructed buildings, and energy-saving renovations of existing buildings, to be designed for energy efficiency. Data reporting specifying the building’s energy consumption and carbon emission are also required. Compared to previous building codes, the regulation puts more emphasis on post-construction buildings operational management (not only the materials and construction process), requires comprehensive measurement and disclosure of energy consumption and carbon emissions, and increases ambition for energy savings through energy efficiency. Carbon emissions: The Code requires that the carbon emission intensity of new residential and public buildings should be reduced by an average of 40% on the basis of the energy-saving design standards implemented in 2016, and the carbon emission intensity should be reduced by more than 7kgCO2/(m2 · a) on average.

Policy: Gas price control measures
Policy_Content: In response to the global energy price crisis, the Polish government enacted measures to ensure consumers benefit from the lowest price applicable to their respective gas supply contracts, from 1 January to 31 December 2022.In addition, gas prices and tariff rates of gaseous fuels cannot be increased in 2022. Gas sellers who fail to comply with the obligation to apply the regulation will be fined. The measure, initially enacted until 2023, is extended until 2027.

Policy: General Law of Climate Change (Mexico)
Type: Loans, grants and other financial incentives;Framework legislation
Policy_Content: This Law, promulgated in 2012, aims to align activities on mitigation and adaptation between the different government entities. The Law establishes following institutions:1) the National Institute of Ecology and Climate Change,2) the Climate Change Council,3) the Inter-secretariat Commission for Climate Change.The Law defines several GHG mitigation targets that directly incentivise the development of renewable energies. These are:1) To generate at least 35% of power with clean technologies by 2024.2) To reduce emissions by 30% by 2020, and 50% by 2050 compared to 2000.The Law creates a fund to channel financial resources (public, private, national, and international) to support actions to combat climate change. Priority areas include energy efficiency projects, renewable energy development, and elimination or use of fugitive methane emissions and associated gas (Article 82). The Law stipulates that federal entities and municipalities should promote the design and expansion of policies and mitigation actions to reduce emissions (Article 34).Relevant to methane, this includes financing and transfer of technology to reduce venting and flaring gas during extraction and distribution processes. The Law stipulates that by 2018, municipalities of over 50000 inhabitants should develop urban infrastructure that does not emit methane, and, where viable, implement technology for electricity generation via gas (Transitory Article III).The law was amended on November 6th, 2020 and in 2022, with additional wording in accordance with the Paris Agreement and the NDC, as well as further clarification for the implementation of the Mexican Emission Trading System.

Policy: GeoSciences IR
Policy_Content: The GeoScience IR project was launched under mission 4 of Italy's National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) in October of 2022. Coordinated by the Higher Institute for Environmental Protection and Research (ISPRA) and financed by the Ministry of University and Research, the project aims to create a new research infrastructure for the Italian Network of Geological Services across 12 areas of study. The objectives of the project are trifold:Work Package 5 (WP5) is dedicated to the creation of information systems for the dissemination of knowledge useful for the sustainable management of soil and geological resources, in particular critical and strategic raw materials. WP5 will create a national portal on solid mineral resources with a focus on critical and strategic materials in support of new procurement strategies. This initiative will also define effective methodologies for minimising the environmental and health impact of extractive activities and explore the reuse of mining waste as a source of alternative materials for industry and construction.

Policy: Geoscience Australia Strategy 2028
Policy_Content: Geoscience Australia was established in 2001 as the merger of the Australian Surveying and Land Information Group and the Australian Geological Survey Organisation. It is Australia's premier geoscientific research organisation, and provides geoscientific advice on critical minerals to the Australian Government. Geoscience Australia’s broader role includes the geological survey’s historical focus on resource development, as well as on diverse topics such as natural hazards, environmental issues, climate change, groundwater research, marine and coastal research, carbon capture and storage and vegetation monitoringGeoscience Australia’s Strategy 2028 identifies the following priorities:

Policy: Germany's Special Climate and Transformation Fund - Transformation of heating networks
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The German government is implementing a support scheme for the construction of green district heating networks.Direct grants are provided to new and existing district heating network operators and operators to finance the construction and the upgrade of district heating networks. In order to be eligible for public support, the systems need to operate on at least 75% renewable energy and/or waste heat.

Policy: Global Methane Pledge Energy Pathway
Policy_Content: In June 2022, the United States, European Union, Argentina, Canada, Denmark, Egypt, Germany, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Nigeria, Norway, and Oman launched the Global Methane Pledge Energy Pathway to catalyse methane emissions reductions in the oil and gas sector, thereby advancing both climate progress and energy security.The Energy Pathway is a critical implementation step of the Global Methane Pledge that will accelerate deployment of the fastest and most cost-effective methane mitigation solutions available today. The GMP Energy Pathway aims to encourage all nations to:Participating countries commit to support these efforts by providing new technical and financial resources and/or by enhancing domestic project and policy action. Countries and supporting organisations have announced nearly $60 million in funding to support implementation of the Pathway through various initiatives, including the World Bank Global Gas Flaring Reduction Partnership, the Global Methane Initiative, International Methane Emissions Observatory and the Global Methane Hub.In addition, the UNEP International Methane Emissions Observatory will work with partners to launch an alert and response system for satellite-detected methane emissions.

Policy: Government Cybersecurity Strategy
Policy_Content: Tanzania's Government Cybersecurity Strategy 2022 aims to strengthen digital resilience by protecting critical information infrastructure and fostering a secure cyberspace.

Policy: Government bailout of Bulb Energy
Policy_Content: The UK Government’s bailout of Bulb Energy incurs a GBP 1.2 billion cost in 2021-22 and a further GBP 1.0 billion in 2022-23, to cover the company’s operating losses.

Policy: Government compensation to oil marketing companies
Policy_Content: The Indian Union cabinet approved a one-time compensation to public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) for the losses incurred in selling LPG for cooking below cost. Between June 2020 and June 2022, international prices of LPG rose by around 300% but domestic LPG price rise was limited by the OMCs to 72% to shield consumers from price fluctuations.The compensation was split among three public sector undertaking OMCs - Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corp. Ltd (HPCL).

Policy: Government grant- Advanced Lithium-ion Batteries
Policy_Content: The Israeli earmarked funding in 2022 for a company grant supporting the development of advanced lithium ion batteries with high energy density.

Policy: Government investment for renewable energies
Policy_Content: Government financing to increase renewable energy contribution to energy mix in order to stabilise electricity prices.

Policy: Government measures to face the energy crisis (1) - Council of Ministers on 4 February 2022
Policy_Content: The Council of Ministers, on 4 February 2022, approved two draft decrees on the cost of energy.The first royal decree releases a framework for the temporary reduction of the VAT rate for the supply of electricity from 21 to 6%. The emergency measure will be valid from 1 March 2022 for four months. However, for technical and organisational reasons, the reduction will be valid for bills invoiced from 1 April 2022.The contracts that are interested by the measure are residential and non-professional contracts, hence exclusively contracts designed for domestic use of energy.Furthermore, the measure is extended to the energy suppliers of the energy on which the VAT cut is applied. These agents bear the 21% VAT upstream and, if not included in the measure, would generally be in a situation of VAT tax credit, given the VAT rate cut applied on residential contracts.The second royal decree concerns the extension of the social tariff for the BIM category (Beneficiaries of Increased Intervention, ) for gas and electricity suppliers. The social tariff entered into force on 1 February 2021 and was limited until the 31 December 2021, as per the royal decree approved on the 28 January 2021. The programme law of 27 December 2021 extends the temporary measure until 1 April 2022. In addition, it was previously decided on 1 February that a EUR 100 premium will be granted for all Belgian households, as a deduction from their electricity bill. The premium will be automatically granted between 18 April and 31 July 2022.

Policy: Government measures to face the energy crisis (2) - Council of Ministers on 14 March 2022
Policy_Content: On 14 March 2022, the Belgian government agreed on a new package of measures to face high energy prices:

Policy: Government measures to face the energy crisis (3) - Council of Ministers on 18 June 2022
Policy_Content: On 18 June 2022, the restricted Council of Ministerns (Kern) agreed to further extend existing measures to support rising energy bills. The following was decided:The measures entered into force on 29 June 2022.

Policy: Government spending for the expansion and modernisation of the electricity grid
Policy_Content: The Romanian Ministry of Energy signed first nine financing contracts with the national transmission system operator Transelectrica in the total amount of EUR 424 million. The funding is provided as direct non-refundable grants for the expansion and modernisation of the electricity grid.

Policy: Government spending in municipal energy efficiency projects
Policy_Content: The South African government is allocating resources to municipalities to perform energy-efficient upgrades in municipal infrastructure.

Policy: Government spending- Energy Production from Household Waste
Policy_Content: The Israeli government is providing company grants to support the development of systems that generate energy from household waste.

Policy: Government spending- Hydrogen Transportation
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The Israeli government earmarked funding in 2022 to purchase hydrogen trucks, buses, and related equipment.

Policy: Government support for electric vehicle charging infrastructure expansion
Policy_Content: Through a dedicated tender, the Israeli Ministry of Energy is financially supporting subnational authorities investing in electric vehicle public charging points. The support provided can represent up to 75% of the station's construction costs.Additionally, as part of the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure's activity for a wide deployment of charging stations in Israel, the government earmarked financial support on 2023 for the installation of 707 ultra-fast and high-speed charging stations on traffic routes.

Policy: Government support for renewable energy capacity additions
Policy_Content: The Ministry of Economy of Estonia allocated EUR 6.8 million to provide subsidies to industrial companies for connection of new renewable energy capacity to the grid. Companies can draw EUR 230 000 per each MWh connected to the grid in the maximum amount of one million euros per beneficiary. Subsidized projects must be connected to the grid within 3 years. The subsidies will be provided by the Center for Environmental Investments (KIK) and applications opened in December 2022.

Policy: Government support for solar PV projects
Policy_Content: The Israeli government is granting financial support to solar PV projects.

Policy: Government support to SMEs
Policy_Content: In 2022, the Romanian government earmarked targeted affordability support for SMEs impacted by the global energy crisis:Additional funds, to be provided to SMEs in the form of State guarantees and grants, were earmarked in 2024.

Policy: Government will introduce a new protection mechanism against high-electricity prices
Policy_Content: The Swedish Government introduced a new protection mechanism against high-electricity prices. Both households and companies will be concerned by the mechanism. SEK 60 billion of the fees paid to state-owned public utility Svenska kraftnät will be returned to customers as a compensation to lower prices. At least half of the amount should go to households, either through reduced charges, refunds, or other measures that lower prices.

Policy: Grant Schemes for energy-efficient retrofits
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The Grant Schemes earmarked €215 million for 2022-2025 to subsidise the installation of roof thermal insulation, photovoltaic system installation in residences, solar water heating system replacement, charging electric vehicles from RES, and energy upgrades for local government buildings and infrastructures.

Policy: Grant schemes of the renewable energy sources and energy conservation fund
Policy_Content: The purpose of the Fund is to provide financial incentives in the form of state grants or subsidy to promote renewable energy sources and energy saving.

Policy: Grant to renew district heating equipment in residential buildings
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The Finnish government enacted a decree setting out subsidies for the renewal of district heating equipment in residential buildings suitable for low-temperature district heating:

Policy: Grants for local energy communities
Policy_Content: Based on an agreement between the Danish government and the Danish political parties in 2021, from 2022 to 2025, grants of DKK 4 million are allocated annually to a financing pool maintained by the Danish Energy Agency for local energy communities for projects related to the energy transition. In 2022, the total support granted by the Danish Energy Agency was of 4 million DKK, of which DKK 1 million was allocated to projects providing information and knowledge to local communities about renewable energy and DKK 3 million to larger projects to develop clean energy solutions locally. Further continuation of the financing pool for 2023 will be re-evaluated.

Policy: Grants for projects of new business models in the energy transition
Policy_Content: Competitive grants for companies to explore new business models for the energy transition, with scoring based on the level of innovation, the scalability, the team’s capabilities and contributions to just transitions.

Policy: Greece National Climate Act - ICE Sales Ban
Policy_Content: As part of its National Climate Law enacted in May 2022, new passenger and light commercial vehicles registered from 1 Jan 2030 onwards in Greece have to be zero-emission vehicles.

Policy: Green Bond
Policy_Content: To accelerate funding for the green transition to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 70% by 2030 compared to 1990 levels, Denmark will issue its first green bond on 19 January 2022 with a coupon rate of 0.00%, and maturity on 15 November 2031, depending on stable market conditions. It will be issued as a "twin bond" with the same characteristics of the country's conventional 10-year benchmark bond in accordance with the Kingdom of Denmark's Green Bond FrameworkThe proceeds from the issuance of the green bonds will be allocated to the green central government expenditures that support the production of renewable energy sources and the green transition of the transport sector.The finance ministry of Denmark announced the green bond would cover government expenses of DKN 10-12 billion (USD 1.52-1.82 billion) in 2022.

Policy: Green Energy Corridor - Intra-State Transmission System Phase-II scheme
Policy_Content: India's Green Energy Corridor - Intra-State Transmission System Phase-II (InSTS GEC-II) scheme was approved by the Union Cabinet in 2022. The scheme aims at grid integration and power transmission of 20 GW of renewable energy projects in seven states - Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.The project will be implemented over 5 years, with the goal of laying 10,750 circuit kilometres of electricity transmission lines by 2026.

Policy: Green Heat Network Fund
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The Green Heat Network Fund (GHNF) is a capital grant fund that supports:- The commercialisation and construction of new low and zero carbon (LZC) heat networks (including the supply of cooling),- The retrofitting and expansion of existing heat networks.It aims to develop and grow the heat network market and to address some of the challenges of decarbonising the UK’s heat sector.

Policy: Green Hydrogen Commercialisation Strategy
Policy_Content: The Green Hydrogen Commercialisation Strategy guides a path and actions towards the commercialization of hydrogen technologies with targets for cost, production, and deployment. The strategy's pillars include investing in R&D and scaling up green hydrogen as a key contributor to early decarbonization through grants, concessional debt, and contracts for difference, to ensure fair allocation of climate finance to this industry. The strategy also aims to establish South Africa as a global key producer through technological advancement and establishing a regulatory framework while fostering the local industry and ensuring a just transition.

Policy: Green Hydrogen National Strategy
Policy_Content: Costa Rica's Green Hydrogen National Strategy is the country's national roadmap to boost sustainable hydrogen in the country.

Policy: Green Loan to support onshore wind farm projects
Policy_Content: EDP Renewables has received a Green Loan from the European Investment Bank (EIB) of EUR 66 million (PLN 304 million) to support the construction and operation of six medium-sized onshore wind farms in Poland. The six wind farms are geographically located mainly throughout the north (Kozlowo, Krasin, Lichnowy, Chojnice and Piatkowo wind farms) and the south (Bogoria wind farm) of the country. The EIB investment will cover close to 50% of total senior debt – the remaining debt amount being provided jointly by Banco Santander and Caixabank Poland.The total nominal capacity of these six wind farms will be of 150 MW.

Policy: Green National Champions
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The objective of the Green National Champions program is to support the development of Hungarian micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with high growth potential in the green economy. The program aims to enhance energy efficiency, promote the use of secondary raw materials, improve water efficiency, and support electromobility investments. By doing so, it seeks to strengthen the technological capabilities of these companies and integrate them more deeply into the green economy.

Policy: Green fund to investment in clean technologies
Policy_Content: In 2022, the government launched a green fund to accelerate Denmark's green transition and in the phasing out of fossil fuels. Overall, DKK 53.5 billion is set aside for investments, with DKK 1.5 billion pledged for 2024 and DKK 3.5 billion annually from 2024-2040.To be eligible, projects need to be related to energy and supply, food and agriculture, buildings and infrastructure, materials and resources or transport and mobility.

Policy: Green steel production support
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The Federal Government allocated EUR 6 million from the Recovery and Transition plan for the development of green steel in Belgium. The grant is part of the Federal Hydrogen Strategy.

Policy: Green transition investment projects
Policy_Content: The Ministry of Environment created in 2022 a grant programme for municipalities aiming at developing green transition investment projects, in the context of Finland's Net-Zero target.The grants are available for renewable development, low carbon hydrogen, carbon capture and storage, electrification and recycling.The initial scheme already granted:The government extended this scheme in March 2023 with additional EUR 2.6 million.

Policy: Greener Neighbourhood Pilot Program
Policy_Content: The Greener Neighbourhood Pilot Program aims to provide energy efficient retrofits to groupings of buildings at the same time. CAD 33.2 million is provided over 5 years to Natural Resources Canada to implement this program in up to 6 community housing neighbourhoods, in order to promote energy efficiency.

Policy: Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards (Air Conditioners above 65kW) Determination) 2022
Policy_Content: The Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards (Air Conditioners above 65kW) Determination 2022 introduces minimum energy performance standards (MEPS) for air conditioners or heat pumps with a capacity greater than 65kW.Performance requirements are based on the requirements from the determination on air conditioners up to 65kW and foresee own schedules.

Policy: Grid-Connected Solar PV Projects Scheme
Policy_Content: The Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) announced a solar bidding program to select private solar producer to build 100 MW of grid-connected capacity throughout the country. The NEA is funding projects at least 1 MW in size and successful bids are to be granted 25 year power purchase agreements.

Policy: Growing our Clean Energy Workforce initiative in Victoria, Australia
Type: Universal energy access;Skills and training;Gender inclusion;Decent jobs;Social standards
Policy_Content: In March 2022, the government of Victoria in Australia announced the AUD 11 million , which includes subsidised apprenticeships, professional mentoring and access to ongoing education for women in the clean energy space. The state found that women are under-represented in the solar industry by a wide margin, accounting for less than 1% of electricians, plumbers, air conditioning and refrigeration mechanics, solar designers and installers, and licensed electrical inspectors. Therefore, the aim of the Growing our Clean Energy Workforce initiative is to increase the number of women working in the renewables energy industry. In particular, the Victorian government will subsidise 50% of the cost of new apprenticeships to support more women entering the industry and provide apprentices a stipend for tools as well as incentive payments every six months. The programme will be managed by two training organisations: Ai Group Apprentice Training Centre and Apprenticeships Group Australia. In addition, the government will also offer free or low-cost training by professional organisations to women currently working in related energy industries, to allow them to upskill and transition to jobs in the renewables industry. As part of the package, the industry organisation Tradeswomen Australia will offer targeted support for women already working in, or considering joining, the solar industry through online workshops, information sessions and professional mentoring opportunities. The skills package builds off the Solar Homes programme launched in 2018, which offers households rebates for the installation of solar panels, batteries, solar hot water, zero emissions vehicles and heating upgrades. The Solar Homes programme more broadly is estimated to have created 5 500 clean energy jobs in the state since its inception.

Policy: Guidelines for management of fugitive methane and greenhouse gases emissions in the upstream oil and gas operations in Nigeria
Type: Process or equipment emissions standards;Flaring or venting standards;Reporting requirements;Leak detection and repair;Flaring or venting restrictions
Policy_Content: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) released these guidelines to establish actions and mechanisms for operators to prevent and control the emission of greenhouse gases from upstream oil and gas operations at new and existing facilities. The guidelines were designed to: reduce environmental and social impacts; prevent the waste of natural resources; and support the achievement of Nigeria's emissions mitigation and reduction targets, including the elimination of routine gas flaring by 2030, and a 60% reduction in fugitive methane emissions/leakages from oil and gas operations by 2031.To this end, the guidelines establish the following requirements for upstream oil and gas facilities:

Policy: Guidelines on State aid for climate, environmental protection and energy 2022
Policy_Content: The Communication from the Commission – Guidelines on State aid for climate, environmental protection and energy 2022 are part of the broader EU regulatory framework under Article 107(3)(c) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. This article permits state aid that supports the development of specific economic activities or regions, provided it does not significantly distort competition within the EU. The guidelines ensure that state aid measures align with EU policies, particularly the European Green Deal, which aims for a climate-neutral Europe by 2050. They establish the criteria the European Commission uses to assess the compatibility of state aid measures with the internal market. Member States must notify the Commission of their state aid plans, which are then evaluated based on these guidelines. While not legally binding, the guidelines are crucial for ensuring compliance with EU state aid rules.The guidelines include several provisions that support recycling and the transition towards a circular economy:

Policy: HRK 1.6 billion for the Croatian TSO
Policy_Content: The Croatian Ministry of Economy allocated HRK 1.6 billion in grants to the Croatian Transmission System Operator (HOPS) for the revitalization, modernization, digitalization and expansion of the power transmission system in Croatia.

Policy: HRK 21 billion energy price package
Policy_Content: The Croatian Government adopted a package of measures in the total amount of HRK 21 billion to mitigate the consequences of increased energy prices. The measures include an electricity price cap of 59 euro/MWh for households applicable to half-yearly consumption under 2500 kWh from 1 October 2022 to 31 March 2023. For consumption above 2500 kWh, households will pay 88 euro/MWh. Companies have electricity prices capped at HRK 0.5295/kWh up to 250,000 kWh half-yearly consumption. Gas prices are capped until 1 April 2023. District heating prices remain frozen until the end of the 2022/2023 heating season. The package also includes a price discount of 5% to 20% per cubic meter of firewood.

Policy: Hainan Corporate electricity consumer subsidy scheme
Policy_Content: In an effort to shield its consumers from the impacts of the global energy crisis, the Hainan Province enacted a manufacturing company-oriented subsidy scheme, based on electricity consumption during the third quarter of the year 2022. The support is distributed end October as follows:- CNY 10,000 subsidy to manufacturing companies consuming 40,000 to 300,000 kWh ;- CNY 50,000 subsidy to those consuming 300,000 to 3 million kWh ;- CNY 100,000 subsidy to those consuming over 3 million kWh.

Policy: Heat Pump Ready Programme
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies
Policy_Content: The Heat Pump Ready Programme forms part of BEIS’ GBP 1 billion Net Zero Innovation Portfolio (NZIP), which aims to accelerate the commercialisation of innovative clean energy technologies and processes through the 2020s and 2030s. Heat Pump Ready will support the development of innovative solutions across the heat pump sector.

Policy: Heating aid system
Policy_Content: The Latvian government has approved a heating aid program to help households cope with rising energy costs. The aid covers various heating methods, including electricity, gas, central heating, wood pellets, briquettes, and firewood. For electricity, the state compensates 50% of the price above EUR 0.160/kWh, up to EUR 0.100/kWh. Gas users receive 50% compensation for price increases, and central heating users get a 50% reduction in service charges above a certain threshold. The program also provides compensation for wood pellets, briquettes, and firewood if costs exceed specified limits.

Policy: Heavy duty electric vehicle ecosystem call for projects
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: In 2022 and 2023, electric heavy-duty vehicles were supported by the Heavy-Duty Electric Vehicle Ecosystems call for projects. This scheme, operated by ADEME, aimed to support the purchase and long-term leasing of heavy-duty electric vehicles, as well as the installation of charging stations adapted to their use. This call for projects had a budget of €65 million in 2022 and €60 million in 2023.

Policy: Home Appliances to Stimulate Green Consumption
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies

Policy: Household Support Fund - 3rd Extension
Policy_Content: In order to continuously support vulnerable households from the impacts of the global energy crisis, the UK Government is providing an extra GBP 500 million of local support, via the Household Support Fund, which will be extended from 1 October 2022 to 31 March 2023.The Household Support Fund, which helps those in most need with payments towards the rising cost of food, energy, and water bills, is administered by local councils in England.

Policy: Household electricity bill stabilisation
Policy_Content: The Government reached an agreement in 2022 with the national power utility company to stabilised electricity prices for households. The 2025 extension of this measure establishes household electricity bill will be capped at 61 euros/MWh (not considering distribution and other related fees).

Policy: Household support fund - 2nd Extension
Policy_Content: In order to support vulnerable households from the impacts of the global energy crisis, the UK Government is providing an extra GBP 500 million of local support, via the Household Support Fund, which will be extended from April 2022 to end September 2022.

Policy: Household support fund- first extension
Policy_Content: In order to support vulnerable households from the impacts of the global energy crisis, the UK Government is providing an extra GBP 500 million of local support, via the Household Support Fund, which will be extended from April 2022 to end September 2022.The Household Support Fund, which helps those in most need with payments towards the rising cost of food, energy, and water bills, is administered by local councils in England.

Policy: Hydrogen Allocation Round
Policy_Content: Over GBP 2 billion of OPEX support was allocated to 11 projects (125 MW of electrolysis) in the first HAR1, with operations to start in 2025. The average strike price was GBP 241/MWh (USD 10.2/kg). Private capital investment of GBP 413 million (USD 525 million) is expected between 2024-2026.

Policy: Hydrogen BECCS Innovation Programme
Policy_Content: The Hydrogen BECCS Innovation Programme supports technologies which can produce hydrogen from biogenic feedstocks and be combined with carbon capture. It forms part of the GBP 1 billion Net Zero Innovation Portfolio, which aims to accelerate the commercialisation of innovative clean energy technologies and processes through the 2020s and 2030s.The programme is in 2 phases: Phase 1 (GBP 5 million) supports multiple projects to scope and develop a feasible prototype demonstration project. In August 2022, 22 projects were selected under Phase 1. Phase 2 (GBP 25 million) takes projects from innovation design through to innovation demonstration.

Policy: Hydrogen Guarantee of Origin scheme
Policy_Content: After a trial period of the HyXchange exchange platform initiative, the renewable hydrogen guarantees of origin (GO) start to be issued from October 2022. The company Vertogas, a subsidiary of Gasunie that already provides Guarantees of Origin for biogas, was designated by the Minister to do the same for hydrogen, and has created a certification system. This system is currently valid only in the Netherlands, and the platform is supported by several companies among which Gasunie, the Port of Rotterdam and the Port of Amsterdam.

Policy: Hydrogen Industry Development Plan (2021-2035)
Policy_Content: The Chinese government laid out a medium- and long-term development plan for hydrogen, for the period 2021-2035. China targets to bring 50000 hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles on the road by 2025 and to build a number of hydrogen refuelling stations. The plan targets green hydrogen production using renewable feedstock resources to reach 100000-200000 tonnes per year by 2025. Besides transport, the plan envisages the use of clean hydrogen in other sectors: energy storage, electricity generation and industry. Currently, China is already the world largest producer and consumer of hydrogen.

Policy: Hydrogen Society Roadmap
Policy_Content: Published by the Department of Science and Innovation, the Hydrogen Society Roadmap sets national ambitions and sectors prioritization on the deployment of the hydrogen economy in South Africa, in line with the Integrated Energy Plan.A total of 70 priority actions have been identified across these high-level outcomes:- Decarbonisation of heavy-duty transport- Decarbonisation of energy-intensive industry (cement, steel, mining, refineries)- Enhanced and green power sector (main and micro-grids)- Centre of Excellence in Manufacturing for hydrogen products and fuel cell components- Creating an export market for South African green hydrogen- Increase the role of hydrogen (grey, blue, turquoise and green) in the South African energy system in line with the move towards a net-zero economy.Among the targets, the roadmap plans to have 10 GW of electrolysis deployed and at least 500 kt of hydrogen produciton per year by 2030; the capacity will increase to 15 GW by 2040. On the demand side, the short-term focus is on the transport sector and on demonstrating industrial technologies, while for the long-term the roadmpa envisions secor coupling and use of hydrogen also in the power sector. This could create more than 30 000 jobs annually by 2040.

Policy: Hydrogen Strategy of the Republic of Croatia
Policy_Content: National support includes incentives like tax reductions, subsidies, and financial support for research and development in hydrogen technologies. A national model for incentivizing renewable hydrogen production, potentially through a contract for difference mechanism, is under consideration. Priority activities until 2030 also include the co-financing of Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles (FCEV) using national resources allocated for zero CO2 emission vehicles. These national financial mechanisms aim to complement EU funding and accelerate the development of a hydrogen economy in Croatia.

Policy: Hydrogen valleys
Policy_Content: The investment aims to support the local production and use of green hydrogen in industry, SMEs and local transport, thus creating new hydrogen valleys (hydrogen districts), especially in Southern Italy, where hydrogen is produced from local renewable sources and used locally. The aim of the measure is to repurpose abandoned industrial areas into experimental units for the production of hydrogen in local RES plants, located in the same industrial complex or in neighboring areas. Through the implementation of the planned interventions, the aim is to incentivize the production of electrolytic hydrogen from renewable energy sources (pursuant to Directive (EU) 2018/2001) or from grid electricity, promote the reuse of unused industrial areas and foster the economic recovery of local economies. The total amount of the Investment is equal to 500 million euros.

Policy: Import tariff inflexion on iron and steel products
Policy_Content: The Mexican government adopted a Decree modifying the import duties of various iron and steel products classified under chapter 72, including wind powers towers (HS 7308.20).

Policy: Important Project of Common European Interest (‘IPCEI') on Hydrogen
Policy_Content: Through the Important Project of Common European Interest (‘IPCEI') on Hydrogen, the European Union is allocating funds to support hydrogen development.The first call for projects in July 2022 focused on developing innovative technologies for the hydrogen value chain to decarbonise industrial processes and the transport sector. In September 2022, the Commission approved funding to support the construction of hydrogen-related infrastructure and the development of innovative and more sustainable technologies for the integration of hydrogen into the industrial sector.In 2024, the 'IPCEI Hy2Infra' was launched, aiming to support the development of electrolysers, hydrogen transmission and distribution pipelines, large-scale hydrogen storage facilities and handling terminals. In May 2024, the 'IPCEI Hy2Move' was approved to support technological innovations.

Policy: Improving the energy efficiency of family houses - Renovate the house
Policy_Content: The investment aims to complete the renovation of at least 25,164 single-family homes with an emphasis on reducing energy poverty while achieving primary energy savings of at least 30% on average. The investment is targeted at owners of older single-family homes.

Policy: Incentive tax on the use of renewable energy in transport
Policy_Content: Since 2022, the renewable portion of electricity consumed for charging electric vehicles on publicly accessible infrastructure can be used by operators as part of the targets set by the incentive mechanism for the use of renewable energy in transport. This mechanism requires conventional fuel distributors to incorporate an increasing renewable portion of the energy supplied to the transport sector in France and provides support for the operation of charging networks.

Policy: Inclusive Recovery Plan
Policy_Content: In May 2022, the Chilean government enacted a package of measures aimed at supporting its citizens against the effect of global commodity inflation, notably for energy. This Inclusive Recovery Plan encompasses policies and pilot initiatives aiming at ensuring the affordability of oil-based products, gas, electricity and heating for domestic consumers.

Policy: Inclusive Recovery Plan- Electricity subsidies (Energy Emergency and Stabilisation Fund)
Policy_Content: In the Framework of its Inclusive Recovery Plan, the Government of Chile implemented a temporary mechanism aimed at freezing electricity prices for households consuming less than 350 KWh and SMEs at July 2022 levels, until the rest of the year. Households registering consumption levels between 350 kWh and 500 kWh will see the increase in electricity prices capped at 5%, and those with consumption levels greater than 500 kWh will see an increase of 15% maximum. Gradual price increases may be allowed over the next ten years.A 10 year Energy Emergency and Stabilisation Fund is set up to administer and fund the Scheme.

Policy: Inclusive Recovery Plan- Pilot Gas distribution scheme
Policy_Content: In the framework of the Inclusive Recovery Plan, the Chilean government and the State-owned ENAP company are implementing a Pilot Programme, distributing 6,000 LPG cylinders to around 3, 000 vulnerable households in San Fernando, Chiguayante and Quintero. The 15 kg LPG cylinders are distributed at CLP 15,200 each. The scheme is expected to reach 100, 000 households end 2022.In addition, the government of Chile stroke an agreement with Argentina to ensure around 300,000 m3 of LPG would be delivered to a number of municipalities (Chillán, Los Ángeles and Temuco) from July of 2022 until September 30, 2023 at a price 15% lower than market levels.

Policy: Inclusive Recovery Plan- Winter voucher
Policy_Content: In the framework of the Inclusive Recovery Plan, the Chilean government enacted the provision of CLP 120.000 Winter vouchers, a measures estimated to benefit 7.500.000 vulnerable citizens registered among existing social support programmes, in addition to persons in a situation of extreme dependence.

Policy: Inclusive recovery Plan- Fuel price subsidies
Policy_Content: In the framework of the Inclusive Recovery Plan, the Chilean government is subsidising kerosen, oil and gasoline consumption so as to limit the transmission of international price hikes, through the use of a Stabilisation Mechanism, financed by a dedicated Fund for Oil Price Stabilisation.

Policy: Increase in AUTOvoucher discount programme
Policy_Content: As part of its March 2022 package entitled "New measures to offset rising energy prices", enacted in response to the global energy crisis, the Portuguese government increased its EUR 0.10/litre fuel subsidy (AUTOvoucher) to EUR 0.40/litre (maintaining the maximum of 50 litres/month) for the month of March 2022.The support is directly provided in participating gas stations. When consumers use an eligible bank card, a corresponding AUTOvoucher benefit is credited to their bank account. In total, consumers can get a monthly benefit of 20 euro.The AUTOvoucher scheme was ended in April 2022.

Policy: Increase in Energy Bills Support Scheme (EBSS)
Policy_Content: As part of its May 2022 Cost of living support package, the UK government enacted a doubling of the support allocated to households via the Energy Bills Support Scheme. Households will get an additional GBP 200 of support with their energy bills through an expansion of the Energy Bills Support Scheme.

Policy: Increase in Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program
Policy_Content: In 2022, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) via the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) allocated USD 385 million to state governments for household energy bills aid.

Policy: Increase in Warm Home Discount scheme
Policy_Content: The Warm Home Discount scheme provides heating bill rebates to eligible low-income and vulnerable households. The scheme helps households in, or at risk of, fuel poverty with direct energy bill payments.

Policy: Increase in grants for thermal insulation of roofs and installation of photovoltaic systems on homes
Policy_Content: Cyprus’s Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry expanded a grant scheme for the thermal insulation of roofs and installation of photovoltaic systems on homes. For 2022 and 2023, the budget increased by 40%, and will be secured by the “Cyprus-Tomorrow” Recovery and Sustainability Plan.

Policy: Increase to subsidy for renewable energy and energy savings 2022 (ISDE)
Type: Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The ISDE subsidy (Investment Subsidy Renewable Energy and Energy Saving) is a yearly recurring program for insulation measures, (hybrid) heat pumps, solar power and connections to a heat network, which runs until 2030.In 2022, the budget of the ISDE is increased by EUR 62 million due to the large number of applications. This means that a total of EUR 290 million is available in 2022. Additionally, a budget of EUR 30 million is available in 2022 for small-scale wind turbines and solar panels.The increase in the subsidy will be available from 18 October 2022.

Policy: Increased budget for fund to support green transition (FSC 2021-2027)
Policy_Content: In August 2022, the Italian government added EUR 500 million to the Fund for development and cohesion (FSC 2021-2027), bringing the total fund to EUR 2 billion. This will finance investments which help decrease direct GHG emissions through electrification, the use of renewable hydrogen instead of fossil fuels, and the reduction of energy consumption. These projects are divided for 80% in Southern Italy and 20% in the Centre and North of Italy.

Policy: Increased supply readiness for goods and services from industry
Policy_Content: The Ministry of Climate and Business issued the Committee Directive on increased supply readiness for goods and services from industry in June 2022 in line with the objective of the Total Defense (Totalförsvaret) 2021-2025 bill that Swedish security of supply should be developed in collaboration with the business community.Under the directive, a special investigator will map the goods and services in Sweden of significant importance for the maintenance of socially important operations or where serious consequences otherwise risk arising if the goods or services are not made available. This will include security of supply for electricity and raw materials.The investigator will undertake the following actions:

Policy: India UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement
Policy_Content: The India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement entered into force May 1, 2022.It provides for tariff elimination for most energy products, including:Rules of origin and local content requirements apply, by which “Minerals and other naturally occurring substances” are considered wholly obtained or produced in the originating territory of the relevant party. All other goods relevant to the above list are considered originating provided:i) Non-originating materials used in the production of the good have undergone a tariff reclassification under the tariff sub-heading level of the Harmonized System; or,ii) The qualifying value content of the good does not exceed more than 10% of the FOB value.

Policy: Indian Railways Energy Efficiency Plan
Policy_Content: The Indian Ministry of Railways announced a five-point Energy Efficiency Action Plan for Indian Railways. The action points are: energy efficiency in equipment and appliances, sustainable buildings, power quality and restoration, data management and monitoring website, and capacity building. A key part of the plan is installing rooftop solar panels on all railway establishments, which can increase renewable energy usage in non-traction operations.

Policy: Industrial Hydrogen Accelerator Programme
Policy_Content: The £26 million Industrial Hydrogen Accelerator Programme provides funding for innovation projects that can demonstrate end-to-end industrial fuel switching to hydrogen. It is part of the government £1 billion Net Zero Innovation Portfolio (NZIP).

Policy: Industrial and Innovation Strategy Horizon 2035
Policy_Content: The Industrial and Innovation Strategy Horizon 2035 aims at enhancing Tunisia's industrial sector by increasing its GDP share to 20% by 2035.The strategy focuses on innovation, technological advancements, and the development of new industries. It seeks to boost exports to TND 36 billion, create 840,000 jobs, and modernize industries to make Tunisia more competitive globally. The plan emphasizes sustainability and fosters private-sector involvement for growth and economic resilience.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13101 Extension and Modification of Credit for Electricity Produced From Certain Renewable Resources
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 extends the construction deadline for technologies qualifying for existing clean energy production tax credits from before 2022 to before 2025, and increases the value of the credit for facilities located in communities that have or had significant employment in traditional energy industries.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13102 Extension and Modification of Energy Credit
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 extends the duration of and expands the list of qualifying technologies for existing clean energy investment tax credits. End dates of the tax credits vary according to the technologies, which now include energy storage, microgrid controllers, and qualified biogas properties.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13104 Extension and Modification of Credit for Carbon Oxide Sequestration
Type: Production tax incentives;Government spending in carbon capture, use and storage
Policy_Content: The US government, in the framework of its Inflation reduction Act, implemented changes to 45Q providing up to USD 85 per tonne of CO2 permanently stored and USD 60 per tonne of CO2 used for enhanced oil recovery (EOR) or other industrial uses of CO2, provided emissions reductions can be clearly demonstrated. The credit amount significantly increases for direct air capture (DAC) projects to USD 180 per tonne of CO2 permanently stored and USD 130 per tonne for used CO2.In addition, the 2022 changes reduce the capacity requirements for eligible projects: 18,750 tonnes per year for power plants (provided at least 75% of the CO2 is captured), 12,000 tonnes per year for other facilities, and 1,000 tonnes per year for DAC facilities.Finally, the 2022 changes include a seven-year extension to qualify for the tax credit, meaning that projects have until January 2033 to begin construction.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13105 Zero-Emission Nuclear Power Production Credit
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 creates a tax credit for the production of zero-emission nuclear power in the U.S.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13201 Extension of Incentives for Biodiesel, Renewable Diesel and Alternative Fuels
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 extends the existing Biodiesel and Renewable Diesel, Biodiesel Mixture, Alternative Fuel, and Alternative Fuel Mixture tax credits through 2024.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13202 Extension of Second Generation Biofuel Incentives
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 extends the Second Generation Biofuel incentive through 2025.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13203 Sustainable Aviation Fuel Credit
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 creates a tax credit for the sale or use of sustainable aviation fuel.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13204 Clean Hydrogen
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 creates a tax credit for the production of clean hydrogen at facilities for which construction commences before 2033.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13301 Extension, Increase, and Modifications of Non-business Energy Property Credit Energy Property Credit
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 extends the existing tax credit for residential energy efficiency improvements and expenses and increases the credit value for certain heat and cooking sources.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13302 Residential Clean Energy Credit
Type: Government spending in storage;Government spending in low-carbon electricity
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 extends the clean energy tax credit for the purchase of residential clean energy solutions such as solar PV and solar water heating, geothermal heat pumps, and fuel cells, and amends the list of eligible purchases to include battery storage technologies.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13303 Energy Efficient Commercial Buildings Deduction
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 amends energy efficient commercial building tax deduction to decrease stringency of efficiency standards and outlines the value of deductions for various groups.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13304 Extension, Increase, and Modifications of New Energy Efficient Home Credit
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 extends a tax credit for contractors who build and sell energy-efficient homes and for homes that meet various Energy Star efficiency standards.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13401 Clean Vehicle Credit
Type: Tax credits and exemptions;Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022, which seeks to reduce domestic inflation – notably brought by the global energy crisis – whilst tackling climate change, establishes a Clean Vehicle Credit of up to USD 7,500 per vehicle to incentivise and accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles. Eligible battery-powered electric vehicles must meet the Critical Mineral and Battery Component Requirement, which establishes the following conditions:

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13402 Credit for Previously-Owned Clean Vehicles
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 creates a tax credit for up to USD 4000 or 30% of the cost of purchasing a pre-owned clean vehicle.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13403 Qualified Commercial Clean Vehicles
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 creates a tax credit up to USD 40 000 (or USD 7 500 for vehicles weighing less than 14 000 pounds) for the purchase of certain commercial clean vehicles.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13404 Alternative Fuel Refuelling Property Credit
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 extends the existing alternative fuel refueling property credit and expands the list of qualifying properties to include bidirectional charging equipment and 2- or 3-wheeled vehicles intended for public streets.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13501 Extension of the Advanced Energy Project Credit
Type: Government spending in electricity networks;Government spending in carbon capture, use and storage;Tax incentives
Policy_Content: The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022, which seeks to reduce domestic inflation – notably brought by the global energy crisis – whilst tackling climate change, extends the Advanced Energy Project Credit for the production or recycling of wind turbine blades, the manufacturing of energy storage equipment and the refinement of renewable or low-carbon fuels. Under the extension, facilities which process, refine or recycle critical materials (as defined in section 7002(a) of the Energy Act 2020) are eligible to claim the benefit. The credit starts at a base of 6% and may amount to up to 30% of the qualified investment in property used in such a project that is certified by the US Department of Energy.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13502 Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit
Type: Government spending in storage;Government spending in low-carbon electricity
Policy_Content: The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022, which seeks to reduce domestic inflation – notably brought by the global energy crisis – whilst tackling climate change, establishes a New Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit to incentivise the domestic production of various components, including applicable critical minerals used in renewable energy generation, storage and related manufacturing.Under the regulation, a tax credit equal to 10% of the cost of production is awarded to the producers of the following applicable critical minerals used in such manufacturing: aluminium, antimony, barite, beryllium, cerium, caesium, chromium, cobalt, dysprosium, europium, fluorspar, gadolinium, germanium, graphite, indium, lithium, manganese, neodymium, nickel, niobium, tellurium, tin, tungsten, vanadium, yttrium and others. Eligible minerals must be produced in the United States.The credit for critical mineral production begins in 2023 and is exempted from the phaseout that is applied to other eligible components beginning in 2030.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13701 Clean Electricity Production Credit
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 creates a tax credit for domestic production of clean electricity with a greenhouse gas emission rate of zero (or lower). Eligible technologies include solar PV and wind.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13702 Clean Electricity Investment Credit
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 creates a clean energy tax credit for investments in zero-emission generation or energy storage technologies.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13703 Cost Recovery for Qualified Facilities, Qualified Property, and Energy Storage Technology
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 enables facilities qualifying for clean energy tax credits to act as 5-year properties under the modified accelerated cost recovery system (MACRS).

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 13704 Clean Fuel Production Credit
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport;Government spending in biofuels
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 1.96 billion for domestic clean fuel production tax credits beginning in 2025, including for sustainable aviation fuels.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 22001 Additional Funding for Electric Loans for Renewable Energy
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 1 billion to provide loans and loan forgiveness for electricity storage projects under section 317 of the Rural Electrification Act of 1936.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 22002 Rural Energy for America Program
Type: Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 1.977 billion to fund up to 50% of projects eligible under section 9007 of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002, especially those boosting applications of underutilized renewable energy technologies.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 22003 Biofuel Infrastructure and Agriculture Product Market Expansion
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 500 million for grants to cover up to 75% of the cost of biofuel infrastructure projects.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 22004 USDA Assistance for Rural Electric Cooperatives
Type: Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 9.7 billion in funding for rural electricity cooperatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, increase energy efficiency, and improve accessibility and resiliency.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 30002 Improving Energy Efficiency or Water Efficiency or Climate Resilience of Affordable Housing
Type: Government spending in low-carbon electricity;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 1 billion to the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to fund sustainability improvements in affordable housing, including electrification, energy and water efficiency improvements, and climate resiliency measures.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 40001 Investing in Coastal Communities and Climate Resilience
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 2.6 billion to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to fund climate resiliency measures, conservation, and restoration of coastal and marine areas.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 40007 Fueling Aviation’s Sustainable Transition (FAST) Grants
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 300 million for grants to support the development and application of low-emission aviation technologies, especially fuels, in the U.S.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 50121 Home Energy Performance-Based, Whole-House Rebates
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 4.3 billion for grants to state energy offices to create and carry out Home Owner Managing Energy Savings (HOMES) programs that provide rebates for energy-saving efficiency retrofits in homes.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 50122 High-Efficiency Electric Home Rebate Program
Type: Government spending for efficient or cleaner technologies;Government spending for energy-efficient buildings
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 4.5 billion for states and Indian Tribes to create and carry out rebate programs for efficiency improvements and electrification in homes, including via retrofits and appliance upgrades.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 50123 State-Based Home Energy Efficiency Contractor Training Grants
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 200 million to support the formation and operation of state-level programs to train and educate home energy efficiency and electricity technicians.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 50131 Assistance for Latest and Zero Building Energy Code Adoption
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 1 billion for grants to state- or local-level governments to update and achieve compliance with more stringent building energy codes.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 50141 Funding for Department of Energy Loan Programs Office
Type: Government spending for energy efficiency and recycling
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 4.3 billion in funding for loan guarantees made under Section 1703 of the Energy Policy Act of 2005.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 50142 Advanced Technology Vehicle Manufacturing
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
Policy_Content: The U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 allocates USD 3 billion for providing direct loans to support the expansion of US manufacturing capacity of low- or zero-emission vehicles.

Policy: Inflation Reduction Act 2022: Sec. 50143 Domestic Manufacturing Conversion Grants
Type: Government spending for low-emissions and efficient transport
